## 20. Visible rollback views (ROLL)

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22; commissioned for 0.4.39.
This amendment replaces opt-in bridging for declared domain widenings and
relaxed unique keys. Existing retention, metering, authority, immutable source,
and atomic activation laws continue to apply. SEC7 owns ordinary check gates
and ranking; ROLL owns deploy presentation and release selection.

### 20.1 Prepared source and selection

Deploy compares every selectable ordinary predecessor, even without sampled
widened rows. A widening without an applicable authored down requires a compiled
rollback view. All needed views must prepare successfully or deploy refuses.
View admission compares structural source domains (including text minima and
formats), nominal aliases, unique keys and caps; it never parses human advice
strings to decide whether a view is needed. A fitting authored scalar down
removes its covered value-domain risk; extraction/renames retain their typed
identity laws.
The compatible join is LLP 3000.000.000.002 §8: optional union, integer and text
bound union with identical format, enum union, recursively joined bounded lists,
and asset size-bound union with identical nominal kind, MIME and once policy.
Nullability and list cardinality join separately. This differs from extraction,
which requires full type equality, including size, optionality and cardinality.
References join only across explicit nominal identity renames. A mixed change
cannot enlarge any current shared-column domain with predecessor-only values:
current read/write predicates may rely on their schema-level impossibility.
The ordinary union view refuses even if that column is not the widening trigger.
A closed alternative may retain the complete current authored source closure
(schema, defaults, programs, helpers, jobs and authority), rather than synthesize
a union. It requires every predecessor table and column under the same spelling,
every predecessor operation name/kind, and current argument domains accepting
every predecessor input under the same closed compatibility rule below. It
retains the exact current domains and values, with no resurrection, translation
or old-only writes. Missing fields/names or incompatible inputs refuse. Current
result semantics are disclosed for old-UI review; current extra operations
remain current-authorized. Native/worker bundle qualification remains mandatory.
Otherwise author a compatible source and truthful migration before deploying. Enum order
and nominal rename spelling do not change this domain comparison. Domain
includes nullability, recursive list-element/cardinality bounds, text formats,
integer bounds, asset kind/size/MIME/once constraints; unsupported or incompatible
domain changes refuse rather than truncate or coerce. No conversion,
zero-money fallback, implicit business default or arbitrary row choice is inferred.

The view retains predecessor operation names and argument contracts, including
existing authored operation aliases under their compilation law (same-module,
no alias chains). Every exported predecessor alias counts as an old name; a
current alias resolves to its actual authored target for input, guard, helper
and authority comparison. Renaming an export never drops its current guards. A current
require can be copied only with identical argument and entire transitive local
binding/helper meanings, lookup predicates and control-flow paths. A changed
unmodeled closure or guard depending on writes refuses. Canonical expression
comparison ignores source locations, never semantics. When a relaxed unique key invalidates an old lookup, or current guards require
an added field on a shared table, retain that field and its authored current
backfill. An affected operation whose current guard/workflow cannot be transported
unchanged may likewise reuse its current authored endpoint under the same closed
input-compatibility rule. Every current added field is retained on a shared table, even without a guard
mention; required fields retain their authored default/backfill and every old
write path must supply them through a compatible current authored endpoint or
refuse compilation. No missing-required-field write is permitted. All helpers in a reused workflow, including write,
return and system-scope dependencies, need identical transitive meanings. An already-authored current endpoint of the same name/kind whose
arguments accept every predecessor input may replace the affected old endpoint;
the initial comparison permits identical argument types, optional widening and
integer-bound widening and enum-superset widening, never narrowing or new required arguments. Retained
current backfill identity keeps its output custody active. This supplies authored
writes for the added required fields instead of inventing defaults; the generator never invents first-row
selection. The replacement's point/limited selection must retain the language's
deterministic total ordering, including its stable id tie-break; a source outside
that deterministic language fragment refuses. Missing or incompatible authored
endpoints refuse compilation.

A generated visible view retains the current forward-migration declaration set
for shared output columns. It does not resurrect a retired predecessor transform
whose outputs already remain current columns in the compiled union. Historical
source and receipts remain intact. This preserves current native values and
migration custody instead of reinterpreting them with a retired input domain.
Transforms needed for fields removed from current source remain subject to the
ordinary truthful-projection and complete-adoption checks.

A generated visible view omits a predecessor-only historical down declaration
when all its outputs remain current columns whose generated domains admit the
current native values. Its immutable original declaration and receipt evidence
remain historical; the view does not reenter that retired projection or restore
stale preimages over native values. Downs needed for removed fields remain.
Exact original-source selection retains its projection/conflict behavior. Writer
adoption still enforces full domains, lifetimes and zero-unacknowledged hiding.

Shared tables retain current caps, immutability, final-existence constraints
and lifecycle guards. Generated source carries authored current constraints,
unique keys, expiry and opening declarations; the compiled view must preserve
current hard constraints, reference-deletion/lifetime shape and sync audience
or preparation refuses. Text constraints follow the explicit domain join, not
a separate implicit relaxation. Schema quotas cannot become weaker merely
because their current rule IR is unchanged. Unsupported structural transport
requires an authored compatible workflow; no arbitrary population choice or
new business default is generated.

Shared tables retain the **current authored authority**, including transition
bindings, read rules, payload guards and field ownership. The compiled bound IR
must equal current authority after declared identity alignment. A release switch
is a view over the same current authoritative rows, never restoration of a
historical database snapshot: deleted rows stay deleted and current values
stay current except declared truthful migrations. No resurrection or replay of
historical preimages over authored current images is authorized. With no
hiding and no domain enlarging beyond current, those row populations remain
the current populations; changing read visibility still follows exact current
authority.
For intentional hiding, IR equality alone is insufficient: §20.2 additionally
checks population-sensitive authority/guards under the actual writer. Removed old immutability/uniqueness
constraints follow explicitly relaxed current constraints. Newer-only tables
retain current rules without promising old clients expose new concepts. Native
or worker dependencies without a qualified authored bundle refuse. Undefined
fields, changed helper closures and incompatible workflows refuse rather than
weakening guards. Nullable result fields and carried/reused guards appear in
an action-focused checklist; successful mechanical adaptations are facts, not
11–42 mandatory decisions. The commissioning author's chosen visible-rollback
contract explicitly permits nullable/wider result domains; these are disclosed
as RESULT compatibility changes, never claimed to retain a nonnull v1 result
contract. Requiring nonnull results would contradict that requested end game.
Names and accepted input contracts remain preserved. Dormant restoration advice
names --restore-dormant.

Removing a defaulted predecessor column requires an authored truthful down.
The initial grammar has no acknowledged-absence escape for removed defaults.
Preview may suggest a cross-table expression from declared references/columns,
but it is advisory source for the author to review, never an inferred business
mapping. A false default is not a reversible representation.

Prepared source is immutable. Each parent manifest maps original target id to
numeric view id, executable digest, changed columns, carried guards and hiding
reason. The parent's full control digest includes the manifest; the view's full
control digest includes its metadata. Prepared views are usable only after the
parent's CAS activation commits and never count as ordinary latest or equal
forward source. Failed parents remove stages/views. Unknown admitted outcomes
retain them for history-authoritative recovery; uncommitted parents cannot
authorize selection. Before either equal-source no-op or retained-source reactivation, prepare the
complete desired view set privately and compare target/executable digest/hiding
reasons with that source's own committed manifest, verifying its entries. A
matching set permits no-op or identity reuse. A missing, stale or newly needed
mapping creates an ordinary registration parent using the same source and full
adoption/CAS validation; no view is selectable before that commit. Output and
JSON identify the equivalent retained source as sourceRelease. Source and old
manifests remain immutable. Temporary desired views are removed on no-op/reuse,
refusal and preview. This also upgrades unchanged legacy deployments without
needed registrations. Later equal source is a no-op once its desired set matches.
Retained-source reactivation and rollback preserve their own registry context.

Resolve the manifest belonging to the active ordinary release, or the
registered parent of the active compiled view, under the command lock. Never
borrow a later deployment's view across source branches: it may carry weaker
guards than the active source. If that context has no mapping, default selection
uses original source with the same writer visibility checks. Bind actual source
digest, expected release and activation revision to the existing CAS. ABA/equal-content switches change revision. Cold, hot,
preview and restart use that actual immutable source. Selection restores dormant
names implicitly, with full data/constraint/lifetime validation. Output and
releases identify original and actual source. --exact selects the original and
reports dormant hiding; it bypasses only default visible-view selection, never
applicable security/strict refusals, authority checks or migration validation.

### 20.2 Writer-enforced visibility

Default rollback, even without a registered view, admits zero unacknowledged
hidden predecessor-table rows. Candidate preview also refuses uncovered hiding
on reverse snapshots. Future bad projections refuse selection under the writer.
Preview populations are privileged retained-row counts, not viewer guarantees.

The initial intentional-hiding spelling is:
`rollback N hides TABLE where COLUMN = null because 'REASON'`.
The candidate column must be nullable, the predecessor column nonnullable, and
table/column spellings identical. N is the immutable original. No arbitrary
predicate, blanket exemption or rename combination is admitted. Its view keeps
the null restriction while joining the nonnull domain: nullable 0..1000 versus
required 0..100 becomes required 0..1000, preserving widened nonnull values.
The nonempty reason travels in immutable metadata and repeats on selection.

Under the actual writer transaction, capture the before image, run full adoption,
then compare every retained hidden predecessor row. Only acknowledged null rows
and the actual hidden-reference closure rooted in them are allowed; unrelated
hidden rows refuse atomically. The closure graph contains only scalar/optional
nominal Ref cells in before-image active rows, as typed by the source schema;
ids are aligned through the catalog identity. An edge qualifies only when its
parent was also active before, is actually retained-hidden after adoption, and
has no invalid reference-lifetime marker. No list, synthetic extraction anchor,
asset, dormant overlay, cascade or set-null declaration invents an edge. A
renamed identity uses its same catalog number. Before-hidden rows are outside
this newly-hidden population; newer-only tables are distinguished. The snapshot
preview is advisory; concurrent writes cannot bypass activation revalidation.
Acknowledgment never changes physical preservation or permits broader read/write
authority. After collecting the actual newly hidden table set, the writer rejects
negative existence authority, reference comparisons that can admit absence, or
population-tainted requirements/control flow. Positive existence requirements
may only become denials. A direct point assertion may discharge absence taint:
if its row is hidden it aborts before subsequent work; its surviving field values
remain unchanged. Writes to affected existing targets require that same exact
point-presence guard. Transitive bindings and compiler-expanded helper bodies
are followed; unknown paths refuse. Tainted branch/loop/conditional-write keys AND persisted write values,
negative/count-based guard dependencies, nested job-query scope and maintained
populations depending on hidden sources are conservatively outside this initial
acknowledgment form. This is a closed syntactic admission check, not an inferred
semantic implication or a finite-snapshot security proof. Explicit reasons do
not bypass it. Source may retain the safety witness in a visible bridge instead.
Ordinary hidden-row occupancy/retention laws remain explicit in the preview;
intentional hiding supplies no promise of automatic forward conflict resolution.

Point-presence proofs discharge taint only for subsequent work in program
order on that exact table/key. A guard cannot justify any earlier tainted read
or write. Mutations/jobs retain their existing atomic transaction law: a later
refusal rolls back all prior writes in the operation, including work before a
point assertion. The population checker does not weaken that transaction law.

### 20.3 Edited transformation outputs

An edited in-place migration output reverses through an applicable down on its
assembled current image, or stays exact if the compiled selected view's full
type/constraints accept that physical value. This never widens a schema per row,
coerces, truncates, null-fills or invents defaults. Otherwise selection refuses.
Original preimage, actual authored newer output, prior computation and physical
old-view presence are separate evidence; edited output never gains native birth.

Forward validates old-view field presence/null/default/lifetime evidence first.
Preserving authored output requires unchanged explicit arguments AND freshly
unchanged computation, including point/existence lookups. Changed inputs require
exact deterministic agreement with authored output or a real conflict printing
competing values. Unedited outputs retain preimage precedence; receipts state
when older views read stale until forward. Repeated and partially retired cycles,
invalid lifetimes, pruned evidence and meter cuts obey the same atomic laws.

### 20.4 Reference renames and asset extraction

Reference renamed-from transports the existing physical cell and reference
lifetime bindings, including retained/narrowed images. It never recaptures a
deleted/reused parent or captured/engine-owned field. Both aliases at once and
unequal destination cells refuse. After identity alignment, nominal target,
nullability, bounds, on-delete and capture shape must be exactly equal; widening
is a separate migration, not part of this rename.

`extract CHILD from PARENT via REFERENCE: {newField: oldField}` is a declarative
migration, not an operation or cross-table rename. It creates one receipt-owned
initial child per source row; child's deterministic id equals parent id in the
child namespace. The child has a required reference to parent with cascade or
restrict deletion; keep/set-null are outside the initial form. Independent active
or dormant destination history refuses. At least one mapped asset is required,
with identical full source/child type. Parent must remove that source asset
column. Other copied fields must be explicitly immutable scalar source fields;
mutable, captured, maintained and nominal-reference copies refuse. Copies must
continue to agree both directions. Other required child columns need authored
defaults. Receipt identity uses numeric parent/child catalog identities and declared column
origins, so table, asset-column and uncaptured reference-column aliases do not
create a new migration or recapture an anchor. Typed schema normalization updates
extraction table/reference slots and preserves source/destination column strings.
Destination admission inspects active rows, dormant rows/cells and competing

   100	fn receipt_image(tx: &Tx<'_>, ct: i64, id: &str, meter:&mut Meter) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
   101	    let item:Option<(i64,bool)>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT octet_length(data),1 FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 UNION ALL SELECT octet_length(data),0 FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 LIMIT 1",params![ct,id],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?))).optional()?;
   102	    let Some((size,active))=item else { return Ok(None) };
   103	    meter.heap((size.max(0) as u64).saturating_mul(64).saturating_add(8192))?;
   104	    let sql=if active {"SELECT data FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2"} else {"SELECT data FROM _dormant_narrow_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2"};
   105	    let text:String=tx.conn().query_row(sql,params![ct,id],|r|r.get(0))?;
   106	    serde_json::from_str(&text).map(Some).map_err(|e|refuse(e.to_string()))
   107	}
   108	fn validate_receipts(tx:&Tx<'_>,key:&str,pt:i64,id:&str,ct:i64,meter:&mut Meter)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
   109	    let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT child_id FROM _extraction_each_rows WHERE definition=?1 AND parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3 ORDER BY child_id")?;
   110	    let mut receipts=q.query(params![key,pt,id])?;
   111	    while let Some(record)=receipts.next()? {
   112	        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
   113	        let scratch=meter.mark();
   114	        let child:String=record.get(0)?;
   115	        meter.heap((child.len() as u64).saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(128))?;
   116	        if receipt_image(tx,ct,&child,meter)?.is_none() || !anchored(tx,ct,&child,key,pt,id)? {
   117	            return Err(refuse("returning extract each lacks its receipt-owned child or valid parent-lifetime evidence; never recreate pruned/deleted history"));
   118	        }
   119	        meter.release_heap(scratch);
   120	    }
   121	    Ok(())
   122	}

   129	fn validate_all_receipts(tx:&Tx<'_>,key:&str,pt:i64,ct:i64)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
   130	    let mut q=tx.conn().prepare("SELECT DISTINCT parent_id FROM _extraction_each_rows WHERE definition=?1 AND parent_t=?2 AND child_t=?3 ORDER BY parent_id")?;
   131	    let mut parents=q.query(params![key,pt,ct])?;
   132	    while let Some(record)=parents.next()? {
   133	        let id:String=record.get(0)?;
   134	        let mut meter=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);
   135	        meter.heap((id.len() as u64).saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(128))?;
   136	        validate_receipts(tx,key,pt,&id,ct,&mut meter)?;
   137	    }
   138	    Ok(())
   139	}
   140	// A suspended declaration has already consumed its historical list. Resume
   141	// validates current child custody; it never replays stale list preimages.
   142	pub(super) fn resume(tx:&Tx<'_>,e:&Extraction,parent:&Table,child:&Table,key:&str,report:&mut super::super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport)->Result<(),RuntimeError>{
   143	    if !known(tx,key)? { return Err(refuse("extract each source list is absent and no successfully applied extraction owns this suspended definition")); }
   144	    let pt=tx.num(&e.parent)?;let ct=tx.num(&e.child)?;
   145	    validate_all_receipts(tx,key,pt,ct)?;
   146	    let (destination,_)=mapping(e,child);let mut count=0u64;
   147	    super::super::activation_walk::walk_metered(tx,ct,crate::rows::adoption::Work::DECODE,None,|id,image,meter|{
   148	        let parent_id=image.field(&e.reference)?.as_str()?;
   149	        if !anchored(tx,ct,id,key,pt,parent_id)? { return Err(refuse("resuming extract each lacks valid captured parent-lifetime evidence; never retrospectively capture an independent child")); }
   150	        let active:bool=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2)",params![pt,parent_id],|r|r.get(0))?;
   151	        if !active {return Err(refuse("resuming extract each requires its existing current parent; preserve narrowed parent authority in a bridge"));}
   152	        let current=receipt_image(tx,pt,parent_id,meter)?.ok_or_else(||refuse("resuming extract each lost its current parent"))?;
   153	        if let Some(through)=&child.through {
   154	            let current=crate::schema::row_image(&current,parent);
   155	            if through.fields.iter().any(|(capture,field)|image.field(capture).ok()!=current.field(field).ok()) { return Err(refuse("resuming extract each would change captured parent authority; use an authored bridge")); }
   156	        }
   157	        for(dest,src)in &e.fields {
   158	            if dest!=destination && image.field(dest).ok()!=current.field(src).ok() { return Err(refuse("resuming extract each immutable scalar copies disagree with the current parent")); }
   159	        }
   160	        transfer(tx,image.field(destination)?,(&e.child,id,destination),(&e.child,id,destination))?;
   161	        count+=1;Ok(())
   162	    })?;
   163	    report.backfills.push(format!("extract {} each: resumed {count} current child rows without replaying consumed source lists",e.child));
   164	    Ok(())
   165	}

   114	    let id = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(v))
   115	        .ok_or_else(|| refuse("extraction asset has no typed ledger id"))?;
   116	    let bytes:Option<i64>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT bytes FROM _assets WHERE id=?1 AND home_table=?2 AND home_id=?3 AND home_column=?4 AND released_at IS NULL",params![id,from.0,from.1,from.2],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;
   117	    let bytes = bytes.ok_or_else(|| {
   118	        refuse(format!(
   119	            "extraction asset {id} has no live source home; never claim or duplicate it"
   120	        ))
   121	    })?;
   122	    let root = tx
   123	        .meta("activation_asset_root")?
   124	        .ok_or_else(|| refuse("extraction requires activation asset custody"))?;
   125	    if id.is_empty()
   126	        || !id
   127	            .bytes()
   128	            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'-' || b == b'_')
   129	    {
   130	        return Err(refuse("invalid extraction asset id"));
   131	    }
   132	    let path = std::path::Path::new(&root).join(id);
   133	    let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&path)
   134	        .map_err(|_| refuse(format!("extraction asset {id} bytes are unavailable")))?;
   135	    if !meta.is_file() || meta.len() != bytes as u64 {
   136	        return Err(refuse(format!(
   137	            "extraction asset {id} byte length disagrees with its ledger"
   138	        )));
   139	    }
   140	    if from != to {
   141	    tx.conn().execute(
   142	        "UPDATE _assets SET home_table=?2,home_id=?3,home_column=?4 WHERE id=?1",
   143	        params![id, to.0, to.1, to.2],
   144	    )?;
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}
   148	pub(super) fn transition(
   149	    tx: &Tx<'_>,
   150	    next: &Schema,
   151	    previous: Option<&Schema>,
   152	    sources: &BTreeMap<String, Table>,
   153	    report: &mut super::adoption_report::AdoptionReport,
   154	) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   155	    if next.extractions.is_empty() && previous.is_none_or(|s| s.extractions.is_empty()) {
   156	        return Ok(());
   157	    }
   158	    tx.conn().execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _extraction_rows(definition TEXT NOT NULL,parent_t INTEGER NOT NULL,parent_id TEXT NOT NULL,child_t INTEGER NOT NULL,child_id TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(definition,parent_t,parent_id),UNIQUE(definition,child_t,child_id)) WITHOUT ROWID;")?;
   159	    tx.conn().execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _extraction_cells(definition TEXT NOT NULL,parent_t INTEGER NOT NULL,parent_id TEXT NOT NULL,column_name TEXT NOT NULL,data TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(definition,parent_t,parent_id,column_name)) WITHOUT ROWID;")?;
   160	    tx.conn().execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _extraction_active(child_t INTEGER NOT NULL,definition TEXT NOT NULL,parent_name TEXT NOT NULL,reference_column TEXT NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(child_t,definition)) WITHOUT ROWID; DELETE FROM _extraction_active;")?;
   161	    for e in &next.extractions {
   162	        tx.conn().execute(
   163	            "INSERT INTO _extraction_active VALUES(?1,?2,?3,?4)",
   164	            params![tx.num(&e.child)?, key(tx,e)?, e.parent, e.reference],
   165	        )?;
   166	    }
   167	    tx.set_meta("version", super::table_renames::VERSION)?;
   168	    for e in previous
   169	        .into_iter()
   170	        .flat_map(|s| &s.extractions)
   171	        .filter(|e| !next.extractions.contains(e))
   172	    {
   173	        let Some(parent) = next.table(&e.parent) else {
   174	            continue;
   175	        };
   176	        let child = &previous.unwrap().tables[&e.child];
   177	        let pt = tx.num(&e.parent)?;
   178	        let ct = tx.num(&e.child)?;
   179	        let key = key(tx,e)?;
   180	        let mut count = 0;
   181	        let inherited = child
   182	            .through
   183	            .as_ref()
   184	            .is_some_and(|t| t.reference == e.reference && t.parent == e.parent);
   185	        let current_parent = &previous.unwrap().tables[&e.parent];
   186	        if parent.rules.read != crate::schema::RuleExpr::Deny
   187	            && ((inherited && parent.rules.read != current_parent.rules.read)
   188	                || (!inherited && parent.rules.read != child.rules.read))
   189	        {
   190	            return Err(refuse(
   191	                "reverse extraction would broaden the current asset audience; preserve current read policy in an authored bridge",
   192	            ));
   193	        }
   194	        for (dest, source) in &e.fields {
   195	            if asset(&child.columns[dest])
   196	                && parent.columns.contains_key(source)
   197	                && parent.column_reads.get(source) != child.column_reads.get(dest)
   198	            {
   199	                return Err(refuse(
   200	                    "reverse extraction would change the asset column audience; retain its current gate in a bridge",
   201	                ));
   202	            }
   203	        }
   204	        if e.each { each::backward(tx,e,parent,current_parent,child,&key,report)?; continue; }
   205	        super::activation::walk(tx, pt, |id, mut row| {
   206	            let saved:Option<String>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT child_id FROM _extraction_rows WHERE definition=?1 AND parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3",params![key,pt,id],|r|r.get(0)).optional()?;
   207	            let child_id = if let Some(id) = saved {
   208	                id
   209	            } else {
   210	                let mut found = Vec::new();
   211	                super::activation::walk(tx, ct, |child_id, child| {
   212	                    if child.field(&e.reference) == Ok(&Value::Id(id.into())) {
   213	                        if found.len() < 2 {
   214	                            found.push(child_id.to_owned());
   215	                        }
   216	                    }
   217	                    Ok(())
   218	                })?;
   219	                if found.len() > 1 {
   220	                    return Err(refuse(format!(
   221	                        "extraction {} parent {id}: several child rows compete for the old asset; declare a truthful bridge",
   222	                        e.child
   223	                    )));
   224	                }
   225	                let Some(child) = found.pop() else {
   226	                    return Ok(());
   227	                };
   228	                child
   229	            };
   230	            let Some(mut image) = load(tx, ct, &child_id)? else {
   231	                return Err(refuse(format!(
   232	                    "extraction child {}/{child_id} was deleted; old asset has no truthful representation",
   233	                    e.child
   234	                )));
   235	            };
   236	            if image.field(&e.reference) != Ok(&Value::Id(id.into())) {
   237	                return Err(refuse(
   238	                    "extraction child reference changed; refusing to rebind its parent lifetime",
   239	                ));
   240	            }
   241	            let anchored:bool=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM _dormant_refs WHERE t=?1 AND id=?2 AND column_name=?3 AND parent_t=?4 AND parent_id=?5 AND invalid=0)",params![ct,child_id,format!("$extract:{key}"),pt,id],|r|r.get(0))?;
   242	            if !anchored {
   243	                return Err(refuse(
   244	                    "extraction child lacks valid parent-lifetime evidence; refusing deletion/id reuse or retrospective recapture",
   245	                ));
   246	            }
   247	            for (destination, source) in &e.fields {
   248	                let kind = &child.columns[destination];
   249	                if !asset(kind) {
   250	                    if row.field(source).ok() != image.field(destination).ok() {
   251	                        return Err(refuse(
   252	                            "extraction immutable scalar copies disagree with the current parent",
   253	                        ));
   254	                    }
   255	                    continue;
   256	                }
   257	                if !parent.columns.contains_key(source) {
   258	                    continue;
   259	                }
   260	                if parent.columns[source] != *kind {
   261	                    return Err(refuse("reverse extraction requires identical asset types"));
   262	                }
   263	                let v = image.field(destination)?.clone();
   264	                retain_cell(tx, &key, pt, id, source, &v)?;
   265	                transfer(
   266	                    tx,
   267	                    &v,
   268	                    (&e.child, &child_id, destination),
   269	                    (&e.parent, id, source),
   270	                )?;

## 2. Language

A top-level declaration describes one table's historical input fields and its
simultaneous output patch:

```quarry
backfill bookings vehicleClass(weight: int, length: int):
  { vehicleClass: 'commercial' if weight > 3500 else 'van' if length >= 500 else 'car' }
```

Here length is stored in centimetres. Arguments are typed historical fields;
they remain in the declaration after the candidate drops those fields. The
compiler binds arguments against their explicit types, not today's table.
The runtime validates them against each interpreted historical row. Output
names belong to candidate authoritative columns and may equal input names:
read-old/write-new. Outputs of multiple declarations on a table must be
disjoint. Names are unique per table. Durable store history keeps one
normalized definition per table/name, including gaps; changing it refuses with a
bridge/new-name repair. A new name denotes a new transformation.

The expression body is an object patch. It uses Quarry's existing arithmetic,
comparisons, null handling, conditional expressions, immutable helper expansion,
and bounded deterministic scalar builtins. Supported text additions are
`before(text, delimiter)`, `after`, `beforeLast`, `afterLast`, `startsWith`,
and `allDigits`. Splits remove the first/last exact delimiter; absent delimiter
means whole text before, empty text after. An empty split delimiter refuses.
Digits means nonempty ASCII digits. Text is Unicode, comparisons and splits
are locale independent. Existing `lower`, `trim`, `slice`, `count`, `sha256`,
`first`, `last`, `at`, `min`, `max`, exact `divide`, calendar/civil transforms
and concatenation retain their normal checked semantics. No randomness,
viewer, clock, minted ids, writes, mutation helpers or loops are admitted.
Identity `id` is never an output. Only scalar outputs are admitted, including new references. Assets, lists,
engine-owned/captured/maintained and lifetime outputs refuse, including fields
owned by a historical source lifetime even when the candidate removes that rule.
Restored narrowed rows retain their individual output ownership, captures and
reference types. Columns added by later predecessor schemas contribute their
own types/defaults only when absent from that archived definition. Overwriting an
existing reference/asset is refused: derive a new reference column so the
existing dormant reference-lifetime ledger owns retirement/restoration.

Point reads use the ordinary `members[principal = owner] ! else NOT_FOUND`
spelling. They require a unique point. A missing asserted point refuses;
ordinary nullable point reads and `exists` retain their explicit semantics.
Historical existence predicates may traverse a metered source range, needed
for wave-17 cross-tower references; they return no row collection. A meter
cut is a refusal, never false absence or an incomplete historical value.
Before evaluating any patch, each unique lookup index validates the historical
population's cardinality with bounded privileged duplicate samples. A different
simultaneous patch making candidate keys unique cannot choose an arbitrary old
match. All reads run as the trusted activation system principal, bypassing application
read rules, against the assembled historical snapshot. Dormant namespaces
remain unnameable. Candidate read indexes are built over that source snapshot
only when their component fields exist there. No JavaScript or app migration
operation receives this authority. All declarations are self-contained: they
cannot read another declaration's outputs in the same activation.

## 3. Adoption and reversibility

The existing activation writer transaction owns this sequence:

1. Assemble retained source rows/cells and their source definitions using the
   existing restoration intent. This includes narrowed rows eligible to return:
   restore their full historical images before evaluation, deferring only the
   backfill output columns' candidate-type checks. Retained reference invalidation,
   source lifetime and audience checks still apply before restoration. Retire
   source-expired lifetimes before any backfill; a transform cannot extend an
   expiry or opening boundary.
2. When leaving a declaration, restore its predecessor-visible output fields
   from saved **output preimages**, separately from its argument inputs. Save
   interpreted old values, including literal defaults/nulls, and absence.
   Added output columns use ordinary dormant retention instead. A different
   current value from both recorded output and preimage refuses with a conflict;
   untouched same-column enum renames restore their exact original value.
   Membership is per row lifetime, with normalized declaration definitions kept
   beside evidence. Removing a whole table suspends its membership rather than
   feeding transformed values back as inputs. Re-entering that declaration reads
   its original overwritten inputs and preserves its current result; selecting
   original source instead reverses it even when the immediately previous schema
   lacked the table/declaration. Ordinary active deletion clears membership.
3. Enter declarations absent from the immediately active schema. Unchanged
   carry-forward and reopening run none for ordinary active rows: candidate-native
   writes are not historical rows. Newly restored narrowed rows receive carried
   declarations too, including a declaration introduced while they were dormant. On re-entry, restored cells/rows are eligible along with
   older active rows. A native v2 row whose absent historical inputs have a
   complete valid restored output image keeps that image. Older v1 rows lacking
   outputs are filled. Declarations must accompany skipped-release source;
   no unseen intermediate transformation is implicitly inferred.
4. Evaluate every entering patch against one assembled source snapshot, with
   ordinary per-row job meters and a paged source walk. Stage output/evidence
   in SQLite temp storage before applying any patch. Recompute the patch on
   re-entry, so changed lookup values count as changed dependencies even when
   declared arguments are unchanged. Compare both saved argument values and
   computed outputs. If unchanged, preserve edited added-column cells. If
   changed, recompute only when current outputs equal the saved result or the
   reversed preimage; otherwise refuse the conflict. Never overwrite a manual
   output edit because another input happened to change. A fully reversed
   same-column output edited during absence also refuses re-entry when its
   current interpreted value equals neither preimage nor saved result, even
   with unchanged arguments. Sparse defaults count by interpreted value.
5. Apply patches and evidence together. Run ordinary narrowing/reference
   closure, projection, complete type/asset validation, indexes, uniqueness,
   caps and maintained-data rebuilds. Transformed dependencies force rebuilds
   even when their declarations did not change. Publish programs, generation
   and release in the same commit. Any error rolls everything back.

Evidence is keyed by table number, row lifetime and the SHA-256 digest of the
normalized declaration/typed IR (no diagnostic locations or whitespace).
It records declared input values, each overwritten output preimage and computed
output. Ordinary authoritative deletion/expiry deletes that row's evidence in
its transaction; id reuse cannot inherit it. Row moves to dormant storage
preserve lifetime. Backfill definitions enter schema/activation identity;
changed rows also set activation population, forcing a fresh generation and
device reacquisition. Public/device schema projections omit all backfill
metadata; devices never execute migrations. A successful evidence installation
sets `snapback4-release-store-6`, transactionally. Unaware binaries refuse that
format even when an old source is selected. Failed installation retains the
previous format. Legacy stores without backfills remain unchanged. Prune previews
backfill preimages separately, with counts, bytes and bounded ids. Explicit
prune deletes their values and keeps only per-lifetime reversal-unavailable
identities. Leaving an overwritten column then refuses with a pruned-preimage
reason: select a bridge retaining present meaning or restore a backup. Active
row deletion clears these identities too. Pruning added-column evidence does
not prevent rollback when no old-visible field needs a preimage.

Dropping a declaration has explicit semantic meaning: leave it by restoring
preimages or refusing conflicts. Keep declarations in every later source
whose view should retain their meaning. Refusals include exact affected counts
and up to five bounded privileged samples. Missing inputs/lookups, output/type
errors, arithmetic/meter errors and uniqueness/cap conflicts refuse atomically;
a widened/optional non-unique bridge plus an authorized repair mutation is the
repair path. A post-backfill-edit conflict requires keeping the current/bridge
source, deciding a truthful old representation, then repairing it before
selecting old source. No automatic fallback turns a new enum value into an old
meaning. Native v2 rows with no preimage retain the parent's existing law:
forward selection may make incompatible present values dormant; rollback
requires representability and refuses with its existing reason. This amendment
does not change REL5's rollback or restoration selection policy.

`deploy --check` uses the existing private disk snapshot, deploy direction and
restoration intent; rollback previews use rollback direction. Later live writes
can change its plan. `backfills` in both cold/hot JSON receipts and exact preview
text reports `table name transformed N rows` or `table name reversed on N rows`.
These are transformed row visits, separate from the parent's disjoint dormant
rows/cells/index entries. They are not additive counts of distinct rows across
different transformations, and do not claim a frozen production population.

Consumed historical references must retain valid parent-lifetime evidence even
when the input column is dropped. Expired predecessor/restored images are retired
before any transform, including ordinary expiry without read-through. Pruning
keeps membership-only tombstones solely for surviving lifetimes; such a tombstone
refuses re-entry requiring lost values rather than treating the row as fresh.

Re-entry retains an adoption-cohort identity with each active row receipt.
All declarations first applied in one activation, including continuously carried
declarations on tables that were never removed, read one reconstructed source
snapshot, including point/range indexes; this overlays that cohort's complete
input evidence and output preimages (including original absence) on current
images. Distinct original cohorts are evaluated separately against their
respective historical overlays, so a declaration introduced later can read an
earlier declaration's already-transformed values. Computed and retained/native output values must fit candidate scalar types and
text minimum/format constraints before narrowing; invalid generated outputs
refuse the entire adoption with affected-row samples. Patches remain staged until
all cohorts succeed, and current row images are restored before applying them.
New declarations use the current assembled predecessor snapshot. Inactive
cohorts restore their own still-omitted input interpretations, independently of
new declarations in that activation, and catch up changed authored inputs. Declared historical arguments consume retained
cells and source definitions even when the candidate omits those columns;
retained parent-lifetime bindings still apply. A native-image exception requires a birth marker for this exact declaration,
a matching fingerprint of the original non-output inputs, and valid, complete outputs;
a new declaration never skips valid old inputs merely because an older
transformation left a retained output. Receipt reference inputs use private namespaced bindings in the existing
dormant parent-lifetime ledger, independently of the live input column. A
retargeted/dropped input cannot substitute its current binding for the saved
reference. Every unchanged saved argument consumed during active or inactive
re-entry validates its private lifetime binding before program evaluation.
Bindings use each restored narrowed row's actual archived reference type
(rather than the table-wide predecessor), even when an
argument is declared as generic `id`. Existing private bindings survive
re-entry with unchanged saved inputs even after the visible column becomes
generic `id`; schema type erasure cannot recapture the same parent id. Reconstruction validates any consumed saved binding before restoring
its value. Original absence is recorded separately from the predecessor's interpreted
value. A physically missing field consumes its source default when present,
otherwise null; receipts retain that interpretation explicitly, preventing
later defaults from changing argument or lookup/index evaluation. Expired sources retire when entering or leaving the
last declaration, including restored table images.

When transformed rows become dormant, candidate output reference types supply
parent bindings even when the predecessor had no such column. Existing invalid
bindings are preserved. If a restored row becomes dormant again, only its
explicitly backfilled authoritative cells update the retained image; original
source definition, other cells and authority provenance stay intact. Forward
selection after rollback reconstructs absent added outputs for that same
declaration before evaluating its arguments, rather than feeding it its own
retained result.

Input omission is stored independently from interpreted null/default values,
both for the current physical lifetime and for each receipt. Ordinary writes
compare interpreted old/new inputs; meaningful edits end omission provenance,
while unrelated writes and default materialization do not. Receipts reconstruct
their original interpretation of omitted fields across later default changes.

Rows inserted while a declaration is active receive a private native-birth
marker keyed by its normalized definition and a hash of their input image;
no original input values are kept in that marker. The same declaration preserves
complete native images with unchanged inputs, including absent optional inputs,
constant transforms and whole-table restoration. Changed native inputs, invalid
present inputs, lost native output images or conflicting other-transform history
refuse with a bridge reason. An inactive overlapping receipt is compatible only
when every overlapping current output equals its recorded preimage; an active
or pruned conflicting history still refuses. Same-column output values belong
to the candidate type, rather than the historical input type, for native rows.
A new declaration name does not inherit another
name's birth marker. Prune retains only native fingerprints for surviving
lifetimes, alongside current omission flags; receipt absence flags are forgotten
with historical values. Delete/reset remove every marker for the ended lifetime.

Source retirement uses the ordinary engine expiry/reference-action closure
under the complete assembled predecessor schema, before any patch runs or
removed table is archived. Only surviving post-action rows enter dormant storage. Restored source
indexes and cap occupancy are rebuilt first; writing-reference groups must fit
the source reservation's live bound. Cascade and set-null effects participate
in this same transaction; restrict or retained-child blockers refuse the entire
adoption. Retired source population forces a new generation so clients cannot
keep children removed by a cascade. Authoritative set-null updates corresponding archived cells/narrowed images
to null before clearing old column bindings, while receipt input bindings remain
independent. An expired
narrowed source is exposed only inside this uncommitted lifecycle phase and
cannot reach a backfill evaluation alive.

Development reset still empties every lifetime's data/history/native/omission
markers, then reconstructs code-derived declaration/input registries from its
retained schema before reseeding; the new identity's rows receive new birth
markers. No release HTTP reset door is added.

Evidence decode is preflighted against
the existing job heap ceiling. Text preview lists private preimages separately
from dormant application rows/cells/index entries.

### Per-column transformed views

A receipt records a `retained_outputs` set independently of its declaration's
active flag. When leaving a declaration, candidate-visible transformed outputs
reverse to their preimages. Outputs absent from the candidate remain transformed
in dormant storage; their set membership survives until reversal or re-entry.
Even an inactive declaration reverses those suspended fields when a later plain
schema exposes them. Whole-table suspension keeps the transformed view intact.

Re-entry preserves the saved preimage for each still-transformed output. A
fully reversed output instead captures its actual assembled source value,
including restored dormant cells and interpreted predecessor defaults, before
applying the patch. Input history and rollback preimages are separate: an input
may retain its original omitted/null interpretation while the latest rollback
view has a literal default. Ordinary writes do not erase omission provenance
when they edit a transformed output from that same original cohort.

An inverse restoring genuine absence records a transaction-local source mask.
Later evaluation cannot fill that absence from the suspended result or a default
belonging to the output schema. The mask is dropped on every exit. Earlier
recorded cohorts' staged patches are replayed into later recorded source views;
fresh declarations still share the untouched predecessor snapshot and cannot
read each other's newly staged outputs. Every decode remains heap-admitted.

Reference arguments copy any matching ordinary cell-lifetime bindings before
restoration consumes that ledger, including transformed reference cells absent
from an archived whole-row definition. Unchanged saved inputs retain existing
private bindings; inferred current bindings cannot overwrite their invalidation.
The stable format is `snapback4-release-store-6`, with schema capability
`release-backfills-v3`. Published 0.4.33's store format 3 upgrades on first use.
Unpublished experimental formats 4/5 and the older capabilities cannot silently read
this evidence layout. Package versions are not changed in this workstream.

## 8. Wave-21 release evolution

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever (EVOL), 2026-10-21; target 0.4.37.
This amendment supersedes the insert-only input policy in §3. Ordinary
writes while the exact declaration is active refresh existing native input
fingerprints. They do not create native birth evidence for migrated rows.
Active forward receipts refresh only actually edited, currently authored
non-output inputs and their reference lifetime bindings. Overwritten historical
inputs, original output preimages, omission interpretations on unrelated
writes, inactive receipts and immutable definitions retain their custody.
An older-release edit does not receive this refresh. At re-entry a changed
input is compatible when deterministic recomputation over the assembled source
produces the exact stored output; an incompatible edit without accepted native evidence still refuses.
Valid native outputs written under the owning declaration remain authored
values, even when they differ from the historical transform. Refresh replaces
the fingerprint, rather than accumulating old accepted images.

Rename destination conflicts consult only physically present or retained cells.
An absent optional destination is absent; interpreting it as null or a default
cannot manufacture a conflict. Explicit present null is still a real cell.

SEC6 owns rule-changing deploy review items, write intent, projection privacy
and client session validation; EVOL does not change those contracts.


A table declares `table observations renamed from behaviors:`. It moves the
same numeric table identity and row/reference lifetimes, never copies rows or
merges independent histories. Both names cannot appear together in a selected
schema. The durable name relation permits old-source rollback and older-source
writes to return under the newer name. Existing independent destination storage
refuses atomically. Indexes, retained type definitions, asset homes and migration
receipts follow that identity; literal values and operation names do not change.
Store format 8 and the release-table-renames-v1 capability fence the new metadata.

`rollback --check --bridge DIR` now writes the selected target's complete source,
loosening only differing compatible value domains to their union with current
source and retaining new authoritative tables with their current rules. It lists
changes and direct target read/write operations on affected tables. It never changes immutable
source or activates automatically. The generated bridge is a new deployable
release, subject to ordinary compilation/adoption. Incompatible nominal types,
new business logic, current guards absent from v1, and old UI assumptions about
null require explicit review; diagnostics and the app-specific checklist remain
visible. A retained new table does not claim a frozen v1 operation exposes it.
No reverse projection fabricates an asset, reference, list element or missing
table. Scalar `down` remains the answer for a truthful scalar substitution;
loosened bridges cover nullable files/images, empty image lists and optional
money without invented placeholders.

Preview causes are recorded by the actual narrowed-population closure: a column
and incompatible value category, or a typed reference to a hidden parent. Counts
may overlap across causes and are schema populations before read rules. New-table
rows have a separate cause. Foresight consults declared reverse writers rather
than calling their old output absent. SEC6 owns review-item resurfacing.

Asset columns (`file`, image/video and asset lists) use `renamed from` as an
identity move, rather than computed scalar forward/down substitutions. The
active and retained physical cells and the ledger's one home move together;
selecting old source changes the public name back, preserving current values.
Both aliases cannot be active together; a conflicting physical/retained cell
refuses atomically. Reference/captured/engine field renames remain excluded.
Older runtimes refuse store format 8; device projections omit migration metadata.

Cross-table historical existence and unique point reads are first-class
backfill inputs under §2's assembled-source, metered system authority. A guide
example must include the source index and explicit row input rather than an
application reconciliation loop. Outputs remain disjoint scalar patches and
all declarations observe the same pre-patch snapshot.

`fileText(file)` is a migration-only deterministic input, accepted in backfill
and down expressions, including through pure helpers. It reads the immutable
retained file named by the ledger, as UTF-8. It never reads an application path
or URL, unverified bytes, arbitrary ids, or a device's filesystem. The runtime
requires an internal migration context and charges the job heap and step meter
before reading at most the ledger byte length plus one. Absent bytes, released
assets, length disagreement, invalid UTF-8 or meter exhaustion refuse the whole
adoption. Preview reads the same original immutable asset root while writing
only its private database snapshot. The feature creates no user-callable
migration operation and does not make arbitrary file contents readable to users.
`nonemptyLines(text)` counts trimmed nonempty lines, including repeated entries
separately; CRLF and whitespace-only lines have their ordinary text meaning.
It is a pure scalar transform; an empty textual list counts zero. A generated
scalar is reversible through the existing output-preimage/evidence custody;
fileText never mutates the bytes or their home. Ordinary new-order byte validation
is outside this release-migration primitive; it receives no invented enforcement
claim from a historical backfill.


### EVOL review clarifications

“Exact declaration” means its normalized typed-IR digest, not a release number.
A declaration can be carried in later source. “Currently authored” means a
column present in that selected schema whose interpreted value actually changes
in an application write; hidden inputs and overwritten migration arguments are
excluded. “Older-release edit” means a write while this exact declaration is
absent. Replacing accepted non-output inputs intentionally forgets their previous
live values: this is live data, not a history of every application write. It
never forgets an overwritten output's reversal preimage. For migrated rows the
parent's dependency/output comparison still applies, with exact recomputation
agreement added for both transformed and fully reversed cells. Native rows with
matching refreshed non-output fingerprints and valid complete outputs preserve
their authored images. A fingerprint mismatch needs full recomputation agreement
or refuses; it never authorizes overwriting a different authored image.

A helper inherits the migration context transitively when expanded. Calling a
helper containing fileText outside a backfill/down refuses during compilation;
raw IR also refuses at execution without the unforgeable internal context/root.
Failure in a forward migration, down, or exact preview aborts that entire
transaction. Preview has the identical job precharge and file validation.
File-read failures never print raw bytes. Output scalars are deliberately
authored data under their destination rules; an author copying file text into
a readable text column must choose its audience explicitly, as for any backfill.
No automatic output or diagnostic exposes the input bytes. Asserted missing
points refuse the whole operation. Nullable points preserve §2's ordinary
nullable semantics only through the author's explicit expression; no missing
point becomes an invented preimage. The database snapshot pins ledger and point
reads; asset bytes are immutable under their ledger id, read at exact length.

Rename conflicts compare a destination cell not owned by the moving alias in
the same surviving row lifetime. They do not compare the source cell against
itself or consult dead row lifetimes. Table moves keep their numeric identity;
independent destination identities cannot be merged. Asset renames never revive
a released asset. A selected schema still validates every moved asset against
the ledger/type. Reference, captured and engine-field renames are diagnosed
before activation, rather than silently losing their bindings.

The bridge's compatible joins are: identical underlying types with optionality
union; integer bounds with the lower minimum and higher maximum; matching-kind assets
with the higher byte limit (file MIME and image-once policy unchanged);
same-format text with the lower minimum and higher maximum; enum member
union; lists with recursively compatible element types, lower minimum and higher
maximum. Other nominal/type conversions are not guessed; they remain target
domains, are listed for explicit typed repair, and receive no promise of complete
visibility. Existing compiler diagnostics and the checklist expose operations
needing adaptation; readers AND writers on affected tables are listed. The
bridge never executes a scalar asset projection: it changes only the selected
schema's value domain over the same retained actual cells. Old nullable UI
assumptions remain an application compatibility check, not a claimed guarantee.
It keeps one alias for a renamed table, selecting the target's spelling; the
other name remains only in the durable identity relation. That spelling routes
old reads/writes to the same numeric row lifetime. It never adds both aliases as
independent tables. Existing target rule/intent text remains byte-identical;
new tables retain current rule text. Ordinary deploy preview reports current
safeguards the target lacks. SEC6 owns rule-review resurfacing; EVOL adds no
blocking review gate or invented safety guarantee.

A cause is either `(table,column,incompatible-value-category,target-type)` or
`(table,column,hidden-parent-table)`. Activation first hides incompatible rows,
then iterates typed reference edges until no additional dependent hides. Only rows physically in the current active `r` namespace immediately before
activation contribute to these preview counts; already dormant rows do not.
Neither source nor target application read rules filter this denominator. A row may have more
than one cause, so cause counts are explicitly non-additive; total hidden rows
are distinct. New-table rows are counted separately. Static foresight compares
possible future domains and declared reverse writers; exact preview runs the
actual activation against current data. Both are privileged local operator
outputs, never per-user query results or public HTTP metadata. Private preview
writes are removed, never published to the live database or generation.


The native and migrated re-entry algorithms are distinct. Native acceptance is
available only when the row has NO forward evidence receipt for the declaration
and has its native marker. A migrated row NEVER gains that marker from an edit.
For each migrated row, every re-entry evaluates the patch again against its
reconstructed inputs and current point dependencies, regardless of whether saved
inputs compare equal. Refreshing its non-output inputs/bindings changes that
input basis, not its `after` computed-result baseline or output preimages. If
fresh computation differs from saved `after`, a stored output equal to the old
computed result, reversed preimage, or fresh computation permits writing the
fresh computation, never retaining a stale value; a different manual output
conflicts. Successful adoption records the fresh computation as `after`. If inputs and computation are unchanged,
the parent's explicit edited-added-cell preservation rule applies. Thus a live
retarget P1 → P2 with O=f(P1) never skips computation at re-entry: it either
recomputes to f(P2) or refuses a conflicting edited O. Backfill is an activation
transform, not steady-state maintained-data enforcement. A native image whose
current input fingerprint matches its accepted native marker instead preserves
its complete valid authored outputs; a mismatching native image needs exact full
recomputation agreement or refuses. These branches cannot substitute for each
other.

Bridge operation listing covers direct lowered Quarry read/write table sites,
including expanded pure helpers. It is a conservative table-level diagnostic,
not a complete dependency proof: indirect rule dependencies, actions, external
workers and frozen UI assumptions require the checklist's manual workflow audit.
The lack of a complete-visibility promise for incompatible type conversions says
nothing about the separate operation-listing diagnostic. No listing grants
authority to deploy or replaces ordinary compiler/adoption validation.

For avoidance of doubt, “active” in visibility accounting is a storage state,
not a viewer's source-rule result. With 1,000 physical active rows and 400 denied
to some viewer, all 1,000 are in the privileged preview denominator. With 600
physical active rows and 400 already dormant, only 600 are in that denominator.
If the target hides 100 of those 600, `hiddenRows` is 100. No source/target rule
predicate is executed to convert that into a per-user number. This preserves the
parent DORM contract and cannot leak to an app caller: the tool is local operator
inspection only.


In the migrated branch, `deps_same` means BOTH input values and fresh computed
patch equal their saved counterparts. If inputs change but the patch equals
saved `after`, `deps_same` is false: the fresh patch is written when the current
output equals saved `after`, its preimage, or that same fresh patch; any other
manual value refuses. Matching more than one allowed baseline has no precedence
ambiguity: each allows writing the same single fresh patch. Only `deps_same`
plus a still-transformed, present output invokes the parent's explicit preservation
of edited added cells. Every successful staged receipt records fresh inputs and
fresh `after`, retaining the correct predecessor preimages.

If both a native marker and a forward receipt for the same digest are present,
the receipt takes precedence: evaluate the migrated algorithm and its exact
baseline/preimage custody. The marker cannot skip that computation. This overlap
is not produced by ordinary writes (which never create a native marker on a
migrated row), but precedence is explicit for retained/legacy state. Pruned
membership is checked first and cannot become native acceptance. Down receipts
have distinct down digests and do not establish native-forward status.

“Affected” for bridge listing includes domain-loosened tables, retained new
authoritative tables, and identities whose table/asset-column spelling moves.
Use the target spelling for a renamed identity, with its current spelling noted
as provenance; never list the aliases as two independent tables. Emit direct
lowered Quarry readers/writers on those tables. The separate manual audit still
covers indirect rule/action/worker/UI dependencies.

An in-place output edited under its declaring source may use a declared down

which already admits it. A failing old type/constraint still refuses; no
per-row widening or invented scalar is allowed. Unedited outputs keep exact
preimage precedence, with a receipt saying when that old view is stale until

computation, selected old physical image and presence. Equal explicit inputs

status. Format 9 fences this retained law, including after selecting old source;

## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
the current credential revision.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted credential timestamps. Staging clock persistence
now follows §12; ordinary dev keeps its process-local offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.

A saved boundary is future-held only when it is strictly greater than the
boundary of the requested effective schedule window. Equality means that the
current window was already processed: report not-due, without consulting wall
time. Repeated advances inside that window and zero-time drains succeed without
allowHeld, including recovery of queued work after a failed drain completion.
Never enqueue the processed window again.
A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
schedule, saved boundary, next unprocessed window and recovery duration to
reach the saved boundary from the unchanged process clock, not from the rejected
requested time. Relative recovery hints in accepted reports likewise use the
actual process clock, including when a disclosure floor is ahead of it.
A held report sets heldUntil to that saved boundary and
nextBoundary to the next unprocessed boundary. Catching up to heldUntil
reports not-due and never re-enqueues the processed window; reaching nextBoundary
fires once. Fresh staging storage and continuing with the original offset are
recovery choices; saved markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.

### Upgrade advice and future formats

Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
guide changes remains available. No ancestor
process inspection or script mutation is introduced.

The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.

### Starter and proof rendering

Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and
partial empty results retain distinct text, with existing freshness and
pagination semantics unchanged. Rename the docs' local ReadState example to
ReadNotice so it does not shadow the export. Password clients omit persona
selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
witness mutate still requires generated API.

Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.
