## 12. Wave-24 loop repairs (DX7)

Commission: Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22; implementer: Codex in sb4-b24-dx7.
This amends §11, LLP 3000.036 §22.8 and the ordinary rule-helper exclusion.
SEC8 owns security questionnaire/dispositions, presence intent, invariant test
coverage and lifecycle advice; DX7 only reports their existing verdicts.
Implementation and tests accompany this amendment; review readiness is distinct
from author acceptance.

### Durable staging time

A staging store owns its cumulative offset and latest explicitly checkpointed
business time. The additive typed metadata record also retains a pending
maintenance pause. Production ignores this record and rejects clock controls;
ordinary dev retains its process-local clock/reset contract. No release-format
change or filesystem sidecar is needed. Store adapters use their existing
metadata transaction and fencing, including Postgres.

Startup resumes at the maximum of wall plus saved offset, checkpointed time,
and the persisted time_audience_clock disclosure floor (LLP 3000.000.000.002
§4), plus the maximum retained commit stamp and schedule boundary even when a
checkpoint exists. A fresh store with no evidence starts at wall time. Unknown
metadata is preserved by ordinary old-binary adoptions; if an older binary or
manual restore removes it, recover time from these retained floors, with no
claim to recover a deleted pause. Explicit startup
offsets (serve --clock-offset and startServe({clockOffset})) are absolute
offsets from wall time, clamped to the resumed floor;
restarting never adds the same offset twice or rewinds saved boundaries.
The resulting effective offset is persisted at startup, preserving the saved
paused flag exactly. This is the maximum of five named evidence values: wall
plus offset, checkpointed now, time_audience_clock, recent commit maximum and
latest schedule boundary (plus an explicitly requested offset floor). Removing
all time evidence by restoring/recreating a store can return it to wall time;
this is the intentional independent-test reset path, never an in-place rewind.
Old binaries do not enforce the pause even when they preserve its record;
downgrade is not a way to run a paused proof under these guarantees. Malformed checkpoints
refuse startup rather than silently resetting. Downgrades to older binaries
ignore this additive record and retain their historical process-local behavior.

Each accepted staging advance checkpoints offset, time and paused=true in the
same transaction that preserves eligible sessions and worker leases, before
publishing the process clock or doing maintenance. E_CLOCK_HELD and input validation precede this transaction. A definite
storage abort rolls back all those effects. Postgres executes the existing
fenced writer transaction containing offset/time/pause and session/lease edits.
An uncertain COMMIT may already have committed: E_COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN fences
the host from further admission/maintenance, then shuts it down. Restart reads
the durable checkpoint before serving; never replay a credential shift to
reconcile it. An uncertain pause-clear may already have cleared it, so only
definite failure guarantees retention of the durable pause. Fault injection
covers both write boundaries. A lost reply is still ambiguous and never automatically
replayed. drain:false, a failed drain and an interrupted drain retain the pause
across restart. A successful drain durably clears it only after due work has
finished. If that final write fails, report an incomplete drain and retain the
pause. Startup writes a checkpoint with zero delta and never preserves credentials.
Each advance computes its delta from the resumed effective clock and writes
credential timestamps and checkpoint in one commit: the checkpoint itself is
the durable completion evidence; there is no separate applied marker. A restart
does not shift already-preserved credentials again. Clock
status/advance reports say the offset belongs to this staging store. Coalescing,
eachBoundary, current-window equality and explicit allowHeld keep §11 semantics.

### Rendered and scrollable text

Mounted text inside overflow:auto/scroll ancestors counts even when outside
the scrollport: it can be reached by scrolling. The selector does not scroll
or change application layout. Overflow:hidden/clip remains a real clip, with
per-axis character geometry retaining only reachable characters. Starting at
each text rectangle, compose legal scroll shifts [current-max,current-min]
and each ancestor clip from inner to outer, independently for x and y; this
excludes unreachable negative-origin text and admits an inner scrollport
inside an outer hidden clip without scrolling the page. Zero-sized scrollports
remain clips. visibility:visible descendants may override visibility:hidden;
display:none and opacity:0 suppress every descendant. content-visibility:auto
counts when browser range geometry exists (unrendered skipped content supplies
no geometry); content-visibility:hidden excludes. Use computed CSS overflow
values, including the browser's visible-to-auto cross-axis conversion. Fixed
and sticky descendants use current geometry only, without hypothetical ancestor
scroll movement; the clip model is conservative for their special containing
blocks and does not claim they can be revealed by scrolling. display:none,
visibility:hidden/collapse, opacity:0 and content-visibility:hidden remain
excluded, as do editable/input/script text and layoutless text. This does not
claim occlusion detection or virtualized content that is not mounted. Existing
normalization, smallest matching element and strict ambiguity remain unchanged.

### Upgrade and gate presentation

Upgrade snapshots count security notes alongside compiler notes and report
pending review gates separately, with unavailable previous gate data stated
honestly for old snapshots. The gate status reflects acknowledgments without
writing them during reporting. A refuted invariant cannot be acknowledged:
check explicitly reports that --ack-security was not applied, leaves review
records untouched and explains that the policy/intent must be repaired.
The JSON field acknowledgmentNotApplied carries the same explanation. The
existing Report::refuted predicate determines refutations (LLP 3000.036.004);
ordinary advisory notes never fail check. Only check acknowledgment paths
write dispositions, and delta reporting only reads them. The CLI takes one
--ack-security ID per invocation; when refuted, that entire single-ID write is
suppressed and check exits nonzero. Old upgrade CLIs invoke the newly installed
check and cannot acknowledge/bypass its gates. The advance scan is bounded
heuristic migration advice, never a security gate; indirect aliases or arbitrary
use(t) dataflow can be missed. Mixed failures show
schema/device remediation before the gate repair/ack command, explicitly
subject to repairing any refutation first. Gate-only upgrade failures name
check --ack-security <ID> --reason '<spec rationale>'; other failures retain
schema/device remediation. An already published old CLI may still print its
old E_UPGRADE line; the new check child must carry the actionable explanation.
The release card records the 0.4.37 CLI's obsolete closed-door/startDev advice.
The numeric-advance candidate scan requires an actual advance call in the same
local expression/assignment as numeric consumption; unrelated operators or
new Date/assert calls elsewhere in a file do not qualify.

### Protected immutable payloads

A column-read-protected payload may be immutable. On insert its supplied value
is validated normally. On every update/existing-upsert, a supplied protected
immutable field is ignored without comparing it with stored data, for every
viewer, including its readers and the system. Its retained value and asset
placement remain unchanged; no upload ownership or placement check runs for
the ignored field because no asset is adopted (amending LLP 3000.036 §22.9).
An ignored newly uploaded asset remains unplaced under the existing uploader
ownership, accounting and collection lifetime; no extra adoption or extension
is created. Immutability constrains update/existing-upsert within one row
lifetime; delete is independently authorized by the table delete rule. It
does not add an undeletable identity policy or prohibit a newly authorized
insert after deletion. The operation still validates supplied input types/bounds; ignoring occurs
before merge/placement, including explicit null for an optional field. Invalid
operation input still fails using schema/site facts alone. An
existing upsert differing only in these fields succeeds with them retained;
absent-upsert still inserts. Compiler advice on an
explicit patch names that behavior using schema/site facts only. Device
prediction retains the old cell or its omission and never predicts the supplied
cell. Ordinary jobs/system updates follow the same rule; schema-evolution
backfills remain the explicit replacement path. Ordinary unprotected immutability retains
its existing contract. Cap/unique/index/authority/derived dependencies on
protected fields remain refused. This input-independent policy preserves
LLP 3000.036 §22.8's noninterference oracle and needs no new device protocol:
the same interpreter runs it on the server and device.

### Audience helpers and hidden probes

Expression-bodied helpers, or a block containing one return, may appear in
table/column rules when expansion is exactly the existing rule grammar.
Arguments are ordinary typed rule terms, substituted simultaneously without
caller capture. Only parameters, viewer and rule constants may be free in the
helper; a helper's focal dot cannot capture the caller's row. Nested helpers
are bounded to eight levels and 4096 visited syntax nodes per rule (including
arguments and each expanded body), refused as E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR on
exhaustion. Direct and indirect cycles are detected on the expansion stack.
Parameters cannot shadow viewer or rule constants. exists is explicitly
allowed and pays the same probes after expansion/inversion as handwritten
rules; ordinary reads are excluded. Simultaneous substitution prevents capture;
cycles,
wrong arity/types, block effects/lets, arithmetic, clock and ordinary reads
refuse with E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR and an actionable repair. No new runtime
instruction, probe semantics, authority or resource allowance is introduced.
Expansion precedes read-through, index inference, audience inversion and
security analysis so every consumer sees the same canonical predicate.

Program exists remains a caller-visible read; rule exists retains its existing
policy probe semantics. N_UNREADABLE_PROBE and N_LOOKUP_FILTERED name the exact
hiding read/read-through rule and source site, including exists directly in a
require. No runtime refusal confirms whether a hidden row physically exists.
Runnable guide recipes demonstrate protected immutable payloads, a role helper
and a hidden parent probe alongside a deliberately minimal readable projection.

### Required evidence

Regression coverage includes repeated startServe/advance/drain runs on one
store, drain:false restart and legacy saved boundaries; no double session
shift; production controls and failed-checkpoint atomicity; mounted below-fold
RN-web text and hidden/clip controls; gate-only and refuted upgrade diagnostics;
real and unrelated advance scan candidates; protected immutable equal/different
patches, upserts, assets and server/device observation equality; helper types,
recursion, capture and authority equivalence; hidden program exists source
advice. Every changed guide snippet executes against the fresh pack. Full
five-crate Rust tests, affected client pool, Mac Studio affected platform tests,
qualify-linux --consumer-only (test.sh is prohibited), published 0.4.35/0.4.37
old-CLI upgrades, refs/docs budget and repository-root checks are recorded in
WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md. No version bump, publication or push.

//! Typed one-child extraction; home transfer is an activation operation.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#20-visible-rollback-views-roll — an asset is moved with its one home.
use super::*;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Extraction {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]
    pub each: bool,
    pub child: String,
    pub parent: String,
    pub reference: String,
    pub fields: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}
impl Extraction {
    pub fn admit(&self, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), String> {
        if schema.extractions.iter().filter(|e|e.child==self.child).count()>1 {
            return Err("one extraction declaration owns each child table; native children cannot be assigned to competing sources".into());
        }
        let child = schema
            .table(&self.child)
            .ok_or("extraction child is not declared")?;
        if self.child == self.parent
            || schema.table(&self.parent).is_none()
            || child.ephemeral.is_some()
            || schema.maintain_for(&self.child).is_some()
        {
            return Err("extraction needs distinct authoritative durable parent and child tables without captured ownership".into());
        }
        if child.columns.get(&self.reference)
            != Some(&ColumnType::Ref {
                table: self.parent.clone(),
            })
        {
            return Err("extraction needs a required reference to its parent".into());
        }
        if !matches!(
            child.on_delete.get(&self.reference),
            Some(references::OnDelete::Cascade | references::OnDelete::Restrict)
        ) {
            return Err("reversible extraction requires on delete cascade or restrict; kept references cannot prove the parent lifetime".into());
        }
        if self.fields.is_empty()
            || self.fields.contains_key(&self.reference)
            || self.fields.keys().any(|c| {
                !child.columns.contains_key(c)
                    || c == "id"
                    || child.engine_field(c)
                    || child.maintained.contains_key(c)
                    || child.sequences.contains_key(c)
                    || child.written_by.contains_key(c)
            })
        {
            return Err("extraction fields must be distinct authoritative child columns".into());
        }
        if self.each {
            let assets:Vec<_>=self.fields.keys().filter(|c|asset(&child.columns[*c])).collect();
            if assets.len()!=1 || !matches!(child.columns[assets[0]],ColumnType::Image{..}|ColumnType::File{..}|ColumnType::Video{..}) {
                return Err("extract each requires exactly one required scalar image/file/video destination; map its historical bounded list".into());
            }
        }
        if !self.fields.keys().any(|c| asset(&child.columns[c])) {
            return Err("extraction needs at least one mapped image/file column".into());
        }
        if child.columns.iter().any(|(c, k)| {
            c != &self.reference
                && c != "id"
                && !self.fields.contains_key(c)
                && !k.is_optional()
                && !child.defaults.contains_key(c)
                && !child.engine_field(c)
        }) {
            return Err("map every required child column or give it an explicit default".into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
pub(super) fn asset(k: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match k {
        ColumnType::Optional(k)
        | ColumnType::List { of: k, .. }
        | ColumnType::ListRange { of: k, .. } => asset(k),
        ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } => true,
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[test]
fn dx8_each_preserves_child_identity_when_the_old_client_reorders_or_appends() {
    let mut e = engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a = handle(&mut e, b"a");
    let b = handle(&mut e, b"b");
    let aid = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&a)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let bid = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&b)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let parent = mutate(&mut e, "add", [("names", Value::Array(vec![a, b]))])
        .field("id")
        .unwrap()
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    let ca = child_for(&e, &aid);
    let cb = child_for(&e, &bid);
    adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
    let Value::Array(mut values) = field(&mut e, "orders", &parent, "names") else {
        panic!()
    };
    values.reverse();
    let c = handle(&mut e, b"c");
    values.push(c);
    mutate(
        &mut e,
        "edit",
        [
            ("id", Value::Id(parent.clone())),
            ("names", Value::Array(values)),
        ],
    );
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(), 3);
    assert_eq!(child_for(&e, &aid), ca);
    assert_eq!(child_for(&e, &bid), cb);
    adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
    let got = ids(&mut e, &parent);
    assert_eq!(&got[..2], [bid, aid]);
    assert_eq!(got.len(), 3);
}

    let next = NEW_EACH.replacen(

        1,
    );

            .contains("read through")
    );
    assert_eq!(e.generation(), generation);
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[(

    )]);
    assert!(
        b.diagnostics
            .iter()

        "{:?}",
        b.diagnostics
    );
}
#[test]
fn dx8_each_preserves_optional_null_and_narrows_removed_old_list_elements() {
    let optional = OLD_EACH.replace("names: [file <=1000] <=8", "names: [file <=1000] <=8 ?");
    let mut e = engine(&optional);
    let parent = mutate(&mut e, "add", [("names", Value::Null)])
        .field("id")
        .unwrap()
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    adopt(&mut e, &optional, 1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(field(&mut e, "orders", &parent, "names"), Value::Null);
    let mut e = engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a = handle(&mut e, b"a");
    let b = handle(&mut e, b"b");
    let parent = mutate(&mut e, "add", [("names", Value::Array(vec![a, b]))])
        .field("id")
        .unwrap()
        .as_str()
        .unwrap()
        .to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
    let Value::Array(mut values) = field(&mut e, "orders", &parent, "names") else {
        panic!()
    };
    values.pop();
    mutate(
        &mut e,
        "edit",
        [("id", Value::Id(parent)), ("names", Value::Array(values))],
    );
    adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),
        1,
        "removed element cannot regain an active asset home"
    );
    for _ in 0..3 {
        adopt(&mut e, OLD_EACH, 1).unwrap();
        adopt(&mut e, NEW_EACH, 2).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(), 1);
    }
}

fn dx8_each_reverse_refuses_populated_narrowed_children_until_loosened_bridge() {
    let wide=NEW_EACH.replace("  names: file <=1000","  names: file <=1000\n  note: text <=100 ?")
        .replace("insert documents {order,names}","insert documents {order,names,note:'a native note'}");
    let narrow=wide.replace("note: text <=100 ?","note: text <=1 ?").replace("note:'a native note'","note:'x'");
    let mut e=engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a=handle(&mut e,b"historical");
    let parent=mutate(&mut e,"add",[("names",Value::Array(vec![a]))]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e,&wide,2).unwrap();
    let b=handle(&mut e,b"native narrowed");
    let bid=crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&b)).unwrap().to_owned();
    mutate(&mut e,"attach",[("order",Value::Id(parent.clone())),("names",b)]);
    adopt(&mut e,&narrow,3).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),1);
    let generation=e.generation();
    let error=adopt(&mut e,OLD_EACH,1).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(error.contains("retained narrowed child asset homes")&&error.contains("loosened child bridge"),"{error}");
    assert_eq!(e.generation(),generation);
    assert_eq!(e.store().asset(&bid).unwrap().unwrap().home.unwrap().0,"documents");
    adopt(&mut e,&wide,2).unwrap();
    adopt(&mut e,OLD_EACH,1).unwrap();
    let current=ids(&mut e,&parent);
    assert_eq!(current.len(),2);
    assert!(current.contains(&bid));
}

#[test]
fn dx8_each_restores_suspended_children_without_replaying_consumed_lists() {
    let suspended=NEW_EACH.split("\ntable documents:").next().unwrap().to_owned()+"\nmutation add():\n  return insert orders {}\n";
    let mut e=engine(OLD_EACH);
    let a=handle(&mut e,b"original");
    let parent=mutate(&mut e,"add",[("names",Value::Array(vec![a]))]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();
    let image=handle(&mut e,b"edited current");let aid=crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&image)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let child=e.store().test_support_conn().query_row("SELECT id FROM r WHERE t=(SELECT num FROM _catalog WHERE name='documents')",[],|r|r.get::<_,String>(0)).unwrap();
    mutate(&mut e,"edit",[("id",Value::Id(child.clone())),("names",image)]);
    let native=handle(&mut e,b"native current");let bid=crate::assets::asset_id(Some(&native)).unwrap().to_owned();
    let native=mutate(&mut e,"attach",[("order",Value::Id(parent.clone())),("names",native)]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    for cycle in 0..3 {
        adopt(&mut e,&suspended,3).unwrap();
        if cycle==0 {mutate(&mut e,"add",[]);}
        adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),2);
        assert_eq!(child_for(&e,&aid),child);assert_eq!(child_for(&e,&bid),native);
        assert!(e.store().adoption_report().backfills.iter().any(|x|x.contains("without replaying consumed")));
    }
    adopt(&mut e,OLD_EACH,1).unwrap();assert_eq!(ids(&mut e,&parent),vec![aid,bid]);
    adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("documents").unwrap(),2);
}
#[test]
fn dx8_each_resume_refuses_retrospective_native_capture_and_unknown_sources() {
    let mut e=engine(OLD_EACH);let a=handle(&mut e,b"known");
    let parent=mutate(&mut e,"add",[("names",Value::Array(vec![a]))]).field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
    adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();
    let without=NEW_EACH.lines().filter(|s|!s.starts_with("extract ")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n")+"\n";
    adopt(&mut e,&without,3).unwrap();
    let b=handle(&mut e,b"independent");mutate(&mut e,"attach",[("order",Value::Id(parent)),("names",b)]);
    let generation=e.generation();let error=adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(error.contains("retrospectively capture"),"{error}");assert_eq!(e.generation(),generation);
    let only_parent=NEW_EACH.split("\ntable documents:").next().unwrap().to_owned()+"\nmutation add():\n  return insert orders {}\n";
    let mut e=engine(&only_parent);mutate(&mut e,"add",[]);
    let generation=e.generation();let error=adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(error.contains("no successfully applied extraction"),"{error}");assert_eq!(e.generation(),generation);
    // An initially empty new-shape backend can own the declaration, then
    // suspend and resume native rows under the same captured lifetime law.
    let mut e=engine(NEW_EACH);
    adopt(&mut e,&only_parent,3).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,NEW_EACH,2).unwrap();

//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

pub(crate) const PRESERVED_SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Authenticated development and staging sessions keep their remaining lifetime across this jump; sessions:expire explicitly tests credential expiry. Unplaced uploads still age. Never replay an ambiguous advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    pub fn staging(offset: i64, floor: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        let mut clock = Self::new(true, offset)?;
        let delta = floor.saturating_sub(clock.now()).max(0);
        if delta > 0 { clock.advance(delta)?; }
        Ok(clock)
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        let draining = options.positionals == ["drain"];
        if !draining && (options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance") {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        let duration_text = if draining { "0ms" } else { options.positionals[1].as_str() };
        if !draining { duration(duration_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?; }
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.deployment_environment().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else {
            let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?;
            // A production listener has no development-token registry entry.
            // Ask its read-only clock door first so the CLI preserves the
            // server's actionable refusal instead of failing token discovery.
            if let Ok((_, status)) = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/clock/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5))
                && status["denied"]["code"] == "E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY"
            {
                return Err(release().to_string());
            }
            let token=crate::verbs::mint_for_dev(address,"operator",1)?;
            (address,instance,Some(token))
        };
        let mut body = serde_json::json!({"duration":duration_text,"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary"), "drain":!options.flags.contains_key("no-drain"), "allowHeld":options.flags.contains_key("allow-held")});
        if options.flags.contains_key("expire-sessions") { body["sessions"] = "expire".into(); }
        if draining && options.flags.contains_key("no-drain") { return Err(input("clock drain does not accept --no-drain").to_string()); }
        let body = body.to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if release_path.is_some() {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,token.as_deref(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev_authorized(address,"/dev/clock/advance",instance.as_deref(),token.as_deref().unwrap(),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            if json.get("now").is_some() {
                eprintln!("clock: incomplete advance report (time already moved): {}", serde_json::json!({"now":json["now"],"fired":json["fired"],"held":json["held"]}));
            }
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

import { identityRequest } from "./identity-request.ts";
import { randomUUID, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import type { ServeHost } from "./proof.ts";

export interface StagingAccount {
  kind: "user"; role: string; email: string; password: string; principal: string; token: string; expiresAt: number;
}
export type StagingSessions = Record<string, StagingAccount[]>;
export type ProvisionedAccount = StagingAccount;
export type ProvisionedSessions = StagingSessions;
export interface SeedAccountsOptions {
  roles: Record<string, number>;
  provision: { readonly name: string };
  /** Service seat authorized by the provisioning mutation. Default operator. */
  service?: string;
  args?: (account: StagingAccount) => Record<string, unknown>;
  /** Whole setup deadline, including rate-limit waits. Default 5 minutes. */
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#2-real-staging-accounts — real credentials and ordinary operator mutations, never system seeding or auth bypass.
/** @throws E_STAGING_INPUT for invalid plans; E_STAGING for production/dev hosts; E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, E_STAGING_SIGNUP or E_STAGING_PROVISION for incomplete setup. Partial accounts/grants may exist; inspect or discard the staging store before retrying. */
async function accounts(host: Pick<ServeHost, "url" | "operatorToken">, options: SeedAccountsOptions, environment: "staging" | "production"): Promise<StagingSessions> {
  // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — custom argument keys override defaults; the seat grants no extra authority.
  const service = options.service ?? "operator";
  const roles = Object.entries(options.roles), timeout = options.timeoutMs ?? 300_000;
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(timeout) || timeout < 1 || !roles.length || roles.some(([role, n]) => !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/.test(role) || !Number.isSafeInteger(n) || n < 1)
      || roles.reduce((sum, [, n]) => sum + n, 0) > 100 || !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$/.test(options.provision?.name ?? "")) {
    throw Error("E_STAGING_INPUT: provide 1..100 accounts across named roles, a mutation handle and a positive timeoutMs");
  }
  const end = performance.now() + timeout;
  const partial = environment === "staging" ? "inspect or discard this staging deployment" : "inspect partial production accounts/grants before retrying";
  const remaining = () => {
    const ms = Math.ceil(end - performance.now());
    if (ms <= 0) throw Error(`E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: setup incomplete; partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
    return ms;
  };
  const request = (path: string, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(host.url + path, { ...init, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(Math.min(remaining(), 30_000)) });
  const config = await request("/auth/config");
  const identity = await config.json();
  if (!config.ok || identity.environment !== environment || identity.development !== false || !identity.password) {
    throw Error(environment === "staging"
      ? "E_STAGING: account seeding requires serve on a fresh deploy --staging with password identity; production and dev refuse before creating users"
      : "E_PRODUCTION_ACCOUNTS: account provisioning requires serve on a production deploy with password identity; staging and dev refuse before creating users");
  }
  const operator = await host.operatorToken(service);
  if (environment === "production") {
    const response = await request("/schema", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` } }), schema = await response.json();
    const named = response.ok && Array.isArray(schema.service_identities) && schema.service_identities.includes(`service:${service}`);
    if (!named) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: WARNING minted service:${service}, but the served schema reports no explicit positive authorization mention for that service identity; rules still decide every operation and provisionAccounts(${options.provision.name}) will likely refuse.\n`);
  }
  const sessions: StagingSessions = Object.create(null);
  for (const [role, count] of roles) {
    sessions[role] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const email = `${environment}-${role}-${randomUUID()}@example.test`, password = randomBytes(24).toString("base64url");
      const {json: reply} = await identityRequest(host.url + "/auth/signup", {
        method:"POST", headers:{"content-type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({email,password}),
      }, fetch, {timeoutMs:remaining()}).catch(error => {
        if ((error as {code?: string})?.code === "E_IDENTITY_TIMEOUT") throw Error("E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: signup deadline expired; partial accounts/grants may exist; inspect or discard this staging deployment");
        remaining(); throw error;
      });
      if ((reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code === "E_RATE_LIMIT") {
        throw Error("E_STAGING_TIMEOUT: identity retry budget exhausted; increase timeoutMs or inspect partial accounts/grants before retrying");
      }
      const session = reply.session as {principal?:string;kind?:string;token?:string;expiresAt?:number} | undefined;
      if (typeof session?.principal !== "string" || typeof session.token !== "string" || typeof session.expiresAt !== "number" || session.kind !== "user") {
        throw Error(`E_STAGING_SIGNUP: signup refused (${(reply.denied as {code?:string} | undefined)?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      }
      const account: StagingAccount = { kind: session.kind, role, email, password, principal: session.principal, token: session.token, expiresAt: session.expiresAt };
      const args = { principal: account.principal, role, ...options.args?.(account) };
      const response = await request(`/m/${options.provision.name}`, { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${operator}` }, body: JSON.stringify({ id: randomUUID(), args }) });
      const result = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok || result.state !== "sent") throw Error(`E_STAGING_PROVISION: ${options.provision.name} refused (${result.why?.code ?? result.denied?.code ?? "invalid reply"}); partial accounts/grants may exist; ${partial}`);
      sessions[role]!.push(account);
    }
  }
  return sessions;
}

   669	pub(super) fn clock_status(request: Request, shared: &Shared) {
   670	    if let Err(why) = clock_service(&request, shared) { return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})); }
   671	    let result = (|| {
   672	        let (epoch, reader) = shared.reader()?;
   673	        let note = crate::dev_clock_store::ahead(&reader, shared.now());
   674	        lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
   675	        note
   676	    })();
   677	    match result {
   678	        Ok(note) => { let now = shared.now(); respond(request, 200, json!({"storeAhead":note,"now":now,"skewMs":now - snapback4_core::now_ms()})) },
   679	        Err(error) => respond(request, refusal_status(&error.refusal(), 500), json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error.refusal())})),
   680	    }
   681	}

     9	fn principal(value: &Value) -> Option<&str> {
    10	    match value {
    11	        Value::Id(value) => value
    12	            .strip_prefix("service:")
    13	            .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
    14	            .map(|_| value.as_str()),
    15	        _ => None,
    16	    }
    17	}

    19	fn rule(rule: &RuleExpr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    20	    match rule {
    21	        RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, RuleTerm::Literal(value))
    22	        | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Literal(value), RuleTerm::Viewer)
    23	            if positive =>
    24	        {
    25	            if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
    26	                seats.insert(value.into());
    27	            }
    28	        }
    29	        RuleExpr::And(rules) | RuleExpr::Or(rules) => rules
    30	            .iter()
    31	            .for_each(|rule| self::rule(rule, seats, positive)),
    32	        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => self::rule(rule, seats, !positive),
    33	        _ => {}
    34	    }
    35	}
    36	
    37	fn expression(expr: &Expr, seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>, positive: bool) {
    38	    match expr {
    39	        Expr::Binary {
    40	            op: BinaryOp::Eq | BinaryOp::SameValueZero,
    41	            left,
    42	            right,
    43	        } => match (&**left, &**right, positive) {
    44	            (Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), Expr::Literal(value), true)
    45	            | (Expr::Literal(value), Expr::Input(Input::Viewer), true) => {
    46	                if let Some(value) = principal(value) {
    47	                    seats.insert(value.into());
    48	                }
    49	            }
    50	            _ => {}
    51	        },
    52	        Expr::Binary {
    53	            op: BinaryOp::And | BinaryOp::Or,
    54	            left,
    55	            right,
    56	        } => {
    57	            expression(left, seats, positive);
    58	            expression(right, seats, positive);
    59	        }
    60	        Expr::Unary {
    61	            op: snapback4_core::ir::UnaryOp::Not,
    62	            value,
    63	        } => expression(value, seats, !positive),
    64	        Expr::Block { body, value } => {
    65	            statements(body, seats);
    66	            expression(value, seats, positive);
    67	        }
    68	        _ => {}
    69	    }
    70	}
    71	
    72	fn statements(body: &[Stmt], seats: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    73	    for statement in body {
    74	        match statement {
    75	            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
    76	            Stmt::If {
    77	                then_body,
    78	                else_body,
    79	                ..
    80	            } => {
    81	                statements(then_body, seats);
    82	                statements(else_body, seats);
    83	            }
    84	            Stmt::For { body, .. } => statements(body, seats),
    85	            Stmt::Check { condition, .. } => expression(condition, seats, true),
    86	            Stmt::WriteTarget {
    87	                condition: Some(condition),
    88	                ..
    89	            } => statements(&condition.setup, seats),
    90	            _ => {}
    91	        }
    92	    }
    93	}

    95	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — minted seats stay ordinary principals; this is advisory schema evidence, never a grant.
    96	pub(crate) fn collect(bound: &snapback4_lang::Bound) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    97	    let mut seats = BTreeSet::new();
    98	    for table in bound.schema.tables.values() {
    99	        for rule in [
   100	            &table.rules.read,
   101	            &table.rules.insert,
   102	            &table.rules.update,
   103	            &table.rules.delete,
   104	        ] {
   105	            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
   106	        }
   107	        for rule in table.column_reads.values() {
   108	            self::rule(rule, &mut seats, true);
   109	        }
   110	    }
   111	    for program in &bound.programs {
   112	        statements(&program.program.body, &mut seats);
   113	    }
   114	    seats.extend(
   115	        bound
   116	            .schema
   117	            .schedules
   118	            .iter()
   119	            .filter_map(|schedule| schedule.service.clone()),
   120	    );
   121	    seats.extend(
   122	        bound
   123	            .schema
   124	            .routes
   125	            .values()
   126	            .filter_map(|route| route.service.clone()),
   127	    );
   128	    seats
   129	}

// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000.000#1 — direct children, file logs and bounded cleanup own proof orchestration.
import { spawn, type ChildProcess } from "node:child_process";
import { closeSync, mkdirSync, openSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const children = new Set<ChildProcess>();
const privateGroups = new WeakMap<ChildProcess, number>();
const groupClosures = new WeakMap<ChildProcess, Promise<void>>();
process.once("exit", () => { for (const child of children) child.kill("SIGKILL"); });
export function register(child: ChildProcess): void {
  children.add(child);
  child.once("exit", () => children.delete(child));
  child.on("error", () => children.delete(child));
}
export interface ProofOptions {
  cwd?: string;
  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;
  args?: readonly string[];

  stopTimeoutMs?: number;
  logsDir?: string;

  secret?: boolean;
  /** Internal: a frontend keeper owns this private process group. */
  detached?: boolean;
  /** Internal: the frontend observes parent death through stdin EOF. */
  livenessPipe?: boolean;
  /** Internal: a keeper-backed group owns npm and other descendant trees. */
  processGroup?: boolean;
}
export interface ProofHost {
  url: string;
  pid: number;

export function deadline(ms: number | undefined, fallback: number): number {
  const value = ms ?? fallback;
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 1) throw new RangeError("proof timeout must be positive and finite");
  return value;
}
/** @throws deadline expires; work rejection propagates. */
export async function bounded<T>(work: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  try {
    return await Promise.race([work, new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
      timer = setTimeout(() => reject(Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms} ms`)), ms);
    })]);
  } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}
/** Attempts every cleanup, even if a preceding step fails or stalls. */
/** @throws AggregateError after every cleanup was attempted; each step has a 10-second bound. */
export async function cleanup(...steps: Array<(() => unknown | Promise<unknown>) | undefined>): Promise<void> {
  const errors: unknown[] = [];
  for (const step of steps) if (step) {
    try { await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(step), 10_000, "proof cleanup"); }
    catch (error) { errors.push(error); }
  }
  if (errors.length) throw new AggregateError(errors, "proof cleanup failed");
}
/** @throws invalid handle/deadline, host stop failure or TERM/KILL reap deadline. */
export async function stopChild(child: ChildProcess | Pick<ProofHost, "url" | "stop">, graceMs = 5000): Promise<void> {
  deadline(graceMs, 5000);
  if (child && "url" in child && typeof child.url === "string" && typeof child.stop === "function") {
    await bounded(Promise.resolve().then(() => child.stop()), graceMs + 10_000, "host stop"); return;
  }
  if (!child || !("kill" in child) || typeof child.kill !== "function" || typeof child.once !== "function"
      || !(child.exitCode === null || typeof child.exitCode === "number")
      || !(child.signalCode === null || typeof child.signalCode === "string")) {
    throw new TypeError("stopChild needs a ChildProcess or { url, stop }");
  }
  if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) { await groupGone(child); return; }
  let done!: () => void;
  const exited = new Promise<void>(resolve => { done = resolve; });
  child.once("exit", done);
  child.once("error", done);
  try {
    child.kill("SIGTERM");
    try { await bounded(exited, graceMs, "SIGTERM"); }
    catch {
      child.kill("SIGKILL");
      await bounded(exited, 5000, "SIGKILL reap");
    }
  } finally { child.removeListener("exit", done); child.removeListener("error", done); }
  await groupGone(child);
}
async function groupGone(child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> {
  const pid = privateGroups.get(child);
  if (!pid || process.platform === "win32") return;
  const existing = groupClosures.get(child);
  if (existing) return existing;
  const cleanup = (async () => {
    const expires = performance.now() + 5000;
    for (;;) {
      try { process.kill(-pid, 0); }
      catch (error) { if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ESRCH") return; throw error; }
      const remaining = expires - performance.now();
      if (remaining <= 0) throw Error("proof process-group cleanup timed out after 5000 ms");
      await sleep(Math.min(10, remaining));
    }
  })();
  groupClosures.set(child, cleanup);
  return cleanup;
}
/** @throws partial, invalid or reversed PORT_LO/PORT_HI pair. */
export function portRange(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string {
  const low = env.PORT_LO, high = env.PORT_HI;
  if (low === undefined && high === undefined) return "0";
  if (!low || !high || !/^\d+$/.test(low) || !/^\d+$/.test(high)
      || Number(low) < 1 || Number(high) > 65535 || Number(low) > Number(high)) {
    throw Error("PORT_LO and PORT_HI must both specify an inclusive range, 1 <= low <= high <= 65535");
  }
  return `${Number(low)}-${Number(high)}`;
}

export function logged(command: string, args: readonly string[], options: ProofOptions = {}) {
  const cwd = resolve(options.cwd ?? "."), id = randomUUID();
  const directory = logsDir(options); mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const logs = { stdout: join(directory, `${id}.stdout.log`), stderr: join(directory, `${id}.stderr.log`) };
  if (options.secret) writeFileSync(logs.stdout, "stdout withheld: secret command (returned only to caller)\n", { flag: "wx", mode: 0o600 });
  const out = options.secret ? undefined : openSync(logs.stdout, "wx", 0o600), err = openSync(logs.stderr, "wx", 0o600);
  const grouped = options.processGroup === true && process.platform !== "win32";
  const executable = grouped ? process.execPath : command;
  const executableArgs = grouped ? [resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL("./proof-command.js", import.meta.url))), command, ...args] : [...args];
  let child: ChildProcess;
  try { child = spawn(executable, executableArgs, { cwd, detached: grouped || (options.detached ?? false), env: { ...(options.env ?? process.env), SNAPBACK4_PROOF_LAUNCH: id }, stdio: [grouped || options.livenessPipe ? "pipe" : "ignore", options.secret ? "pipe" : out!, err, ...(grouped ? ["ipc" as const] : [])] }); }
  finally { if (out !== undefined) closeSync(out); closeSync(err); }
  if (grouped && child.pid) privateGroups.set(child, child.pid);
  // Secret stdout never reaches a file, even briefly. Callers still receive it.
  let stdout = "";
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", chunk => { stdout += chunk; });
  register(child);
  child.stdin?.on("error", () => {});
  let error: Error | undefined;
  let actualPid = child.pid;
  let actualCode: number | null = null;
  let actualSignal: NodeJS.Signals | null = null;
  let startedResolve!: () => void, startedReject!: (error: Error) => void, startedSettled = false;
  const started = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => { startedResolve = resolve; startedReject = reject; });
  void started.catch(() => {}); // command() observes close/error instead; host startup awaits this promise.
  const didStart = () => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedResolve(); } };
  const failedStart = (value: unknown) => { if (!startedSettled) { startedSettled = true; startedReject(value instanceof Error ? value : Error(String(value))); } };
  if (!grouped) didStart();
  child.on("message", message => {
    const event = message as {type?:string;pid?:number;code?:number|null;signal?:NodeJS.Signals|null;error?:string};
    if (event.type === "started" && typeof event.pid === "number") { actualPid = event.pid; didStart(); }
    if (event.type === "result") { actualCode = event.code ?? null; actualSignal = event.signal ?? null; if (event.error) error = Error(event.error); }
  });
  child.on("error", value => { error = value; failedStart(value); });
  const closed = new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => child.once("close", () => {
    failedStart(error ?? Error("proof command exited before its process-group handshake"));
    groupGone(child).then(resolve,reject);
  }));
  return { child, logs, id, closed, started, pid: () => actualPid, code: () => grouped ? actualCode : child.exitCode, signal: () => grouped ? actualSignal : child.signalCode, stdout: () => options.secret ? stdout : logText(logs.stdout), error: () => error };
}
export const logText = (path: string): string => readFileSync(path, "utf8");
export async function ready(run: ReturnType<typeof logged>, parse: (line: string) => string | undefined, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string> {
  const end = performance.now() + timeoutMs;
  let outAt = 0, errAt = 0;
  while (performance.now() < end) {
    if (run.error()) throw run.error();
    if (run.child.exitCode !== null || run.child.signalCode !== null) {
      throw Error(`proof child exited before ready (${run.child.exitCode ?? run.child.signalCode}); ${run.logs.stderr}\n${logText(run.logs.stderr).slice(-4000)}`);
    }
    for (const [path, offset, stream] of [[run.logs.stdout, outAt, "out"], [run.logs.stderr, errAt, "err"]] as const) {
      const text = logText(path);
      const complete = text.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1;
      for (const line of text.slice(offset, complete).split("\n")) {
        const url = parse(stripVTControlCharacters(line).trim());
        if (url) return url;
      }
      if (stream === "out") outAt = complete; else errAt = complete;
    }
    await sleep(25);
  }
  throw Error(`proof child ready timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms; logs: ${run.logs.stdout}, ${run.logs.stderr}`);
}

    26	        (A::Json{max_bytes:a},A::Json{max_bytes:b})=>b>=a,
    27	        (A::File{max:a,types:at},A::File{max:b,types:bt})=>b>=a && snapback4_core::assets::FILE_TYPES.iter().all(|t|!snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(at,t)||snapback4_core::assets::file_accepts(bt,t)),
    28	        (A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..},A::List{..}|A::ListRange{..})=> {
    29	            let parts=|t:&A|match t {A::List{of,max}=>(0,*max,of.clone()),A::ListRange{of,min,max}=>(*min,*max,of.clone()),_=>unreachable!()};
    30	            let (a,b,at)=parts(old);let(c,d,bt)=parts(new);
    31	            c<=a && d>=b && match(at,bt){(_,None)=>true,(Some(a),Some(b))=>accepts_in(&a,&b,old_bound,new_bound),_=>false}
    32	        }
    33	        _=>false,
    34	    }
    35	}
    36	
    37	#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    38	enum ResultChange { Same, Additive, Changed }
    39	
    40	fn combine(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item=ResultChange>, extra: bool) -> ResultChange {
    41	    let mut additive=extra;
    42	    for field in fields {
    43	        match field {ResultChange::Changed=>return ResultChange::Changed,ResultChange::Additive=>additive=true,ResultChange::Same=>{}}
    44	    }
    45	    if additive {ResultChange::Additive} else {ResultChange::Same}
    46	}
    47	
    48	fn table_fields(name: &str, bound: &Bound) -> Option<BTreeMap<String,String>> {
    49	    let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
    50	    let table=schema.tables.get(name)?;
    51	    Some(table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n.clone(),format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect())
    52	}
    53	
    54	fn map_change<T>(old: &BTreeMap<String,T>, new: &BTreeMap<String,T>, compare: impl Fn(&T,&T)->ResultChange) -> ResultChange {
    55	    combine(old.iter().map(|(name,old)|new.get(name).map(|new|compare(old,new)).unwrap_or(ResultChange::Changed)),new.len()>old.len())
    56	}
    57	
    58	fn result_change(old: &Ty, new: &Ty, old_bound: &Bound, new_bound: &Bound) -> ResultChange {
    59	    if result(old,old_bound)==result(new,new_bound) {return ResultChange::Same;}
    60	    match (old,new) {
    61	        (Ty::Optional(a),Ty::Optional(b))|(Ty::Omittable(a),Ty::Omittable(b))
    62	        |(Ty::List(a,_),Ty::List(b,_))|(Ty::Collection(a,_),Ty::Collection(b,_))=>result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound),
    63	        (Ty::Object(a)|Ty::RowShape(a)|Ty::RowObject(a),Ty::Object(b)|Ty::RowShape(b)|Ty::RowObject(b))=>map_change(a,b,|a,b|result_change(a,b,old_bound,new_bound)),
    64	        (Ty::Row(a)|Ty::WriteRow(a)|Ty::Page(a,_),Ty::Row(b)|Ty::WriteRow(b)|Ty::Page(b,_)) if a==b=>{
    65	            let (Some(a),Some(b))=(table_fields(a,old_bound),table_fields(b,new_bound)) else{return ResultChange::Changed;};
    66	            combine(a.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if b.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),b.len()>a.len())
    67	        }
    68	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    69	    }
    70	}
    71	
    72	fn action_result_change(old: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>, new: Option<&BTreeMap<String,A>>) -> ResultChange {
    73	    match (old,new) {
    74	        (None,None)=>ResultChange::Same,
    75	        (Some(old),Some(new))=>combine(old.iter().map(|(name,kind)|if new.get(name)==Some(kind){ResultChange::Same}else{ResultChange::Changed}),new.len()>old.len()),
    76	        _=>ResultChange::Changed,
    77	    }
    78	}
    79	
    80	pub fn is_note(line: &str) -> bool { line.contains(": RESULT NOTE:") }
    81	
    82	fn result(ty: &Ty, bound: &Bound) -> String {
    83	    match ty {
    84	        Ty::Row(name)|Ty::WriteRow(name)|Ty::Page(name,_)=> {
    85	            let schema=bound.schema.public_projection();
    86	            if let Some(table)=schema.tables.get(name) {
    87	                let fields: BTreeMap<_,_>=table.columns.iter().filter(|(n,_)|!table.engine_field(n)).map(|(n,t)|(n,format!("{t:?};private={};constraints={:?}",table.read_optional(n),table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field,..} if field==n)).collect::<Vec<_>>()))).collect();
    88	                format!("{}:{name}:{fields:?}",if matches!(ty,Ty::Page(..)){"page"}else{"row"})
    89	            } else {format!("{ty:?}")}
    90	        }
    91	        Ty::Optional(t)=>format!("optional {}",result(t,bound)),
    92	        Ty::Omittable(t)=>format!("omittable {}",result(t,bound)),
    93	        Ty::List(t,_)|Ty::Collection(t,_)=>format!("list {}",result(t,bound)),
    94	        Ty::Object(fields)|Ty::RowShape(fields)|Ty::RowObject(fields)=>format!("object {:?}",fields.iter().map(|(n,t)|(n,result(t,bound))).collect::<BTreeMap<_,_>>()),
    95	        Ty::Text(max)=>format!("text<={max}"),
    96	        _=>format!("{ty:?}"),
    97	    }
    98	}
    99	
   100	fn refusals(p: &BoundProgram) -> Vec<String> {
   101	    fn walk(v: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
   102	        match v {
   103	            serde_json::Value::Object(o)=> {
   104	                if let Some(r)=o.get("Require") {out.push(format!("{}:{}",r["code"],r["message"]));}
   105	                for v in o.values(){walk(v,out);}
   106	            }
   107	            serde_json::Value::Array(a)=>for v in a{walk(v,out);},
   108	            _=>{}
   109	        }
   110	    }
   111	    let mut out=Vec::new();walk(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program.body).unwrap(),&mut out);out
   112	}
   113	
   114	/// Reports are advisory: compatibility cannot license calls or prove unchanged behavior.
   115	pub fn compare(old: &Bound, new: &Bound, label: &str) -> Vec<String> {
   116	    let mut lines=Vec::new();
   117	    for before in old.programs.iter().filter(|p|p.program.kind!=ProgramKind::Job) {
   118	        let name=&before.program.name;
   119	        let prefix=format!("old-client compatibility ({label}), operation {name}");
   120	        let Some(after)=new.programs.iter().find(|p|p.program.name==*name) else {
   121	            lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed operation; old calls get E_OP; keep `alias {name} = replacement` for a same-module query/mutation, or retain a wrapper"));continue;
   122	        };
   123	        if before.program.kind!=after.program.kind {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: operation kind changed; retain the old endpoint kind"));continue;}
   124	        let compatible_rename = |new_name: &str, new_kind: &A| before.program.args.iter().find(|(old_name, old_kind)|
   125	            !after.program.args.contains_key(*old_name) && accepts_in(old_kind,new_kind,Some(old),Some(new)) &&
   126	            after.program.arg_aliases.get(*old_name).is_none_or(|canonical|canonical==new_name));
   127	        for (arg,kind) in &after.program.args {
   128	            if before.program.args.contains_key(arg) { continue; }
   129	            if let Some((old_arg,old_kind))=before.program.args.iter().find(|(old,_)|after.program.arg_aliases.get(*old)==Some(arg)) {
   130	                if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new)) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {old_arg} → {arg} narrows the old input domain ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper"));}
   131	            } else if !matches!(kind,A::Optional(_)) {
   132	                if let Some((old,_))=compatible_rename(arg,kind) {
   133	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: required argument {old} appears renamed to {arg}; old calls get E_INPUT; declare `{arg}: <new type> alias {old}` if it is the same value, or retain a compatible wrapper"));
   134	                } else {
   135	                    lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: clients calling without new required argument {arg} get E_INPUT; give {arg} a fitting `default <literal>` or retain a compatible wrapper"));
   136	                }
   137	            }
   138	        }
   139	        for (arg,kind) in &before.program.args {
   140	            match after.program.args.get(arg) {
   141	                None if after.program.arg_aliases.contains_key(arg)=>{
   142	                    let next=&after.program.args[&after.program.arg_aliases[arg]];
   143	                    if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new)){lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: aliased argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); retain its old input domain"));}
   144	                },
   145	                None if after.program.args.iter().any(|(new,next)|compatible_rename(new,next).is_some_and(|(old,_)|old==arg))=>{},
   146	                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument {arg}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain `{arg}: <old type> deprecated` on a query/mutation")),
   147	                Some(next) if !accepts_in(kind,next,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument {arg} retyped or narrowed ({kind:?} → {next:?}); old values may get E_INPUT; retain the old input domain or a compatible wrapper")),
   148	                _=>{}
   149	            }
   150	        }
   151	        for (alias,canonical) in &before.program.arg_aliases {
   152	            let old_kind=&before.program.args[canonical];
   153	            let next=after.program.args.get(alias).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(alias).and_then(|name|after.program.args.get(name)));
   154	            match next {
   155	                None=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: removed argument alias {alias}; old calls sending it get E_INPUT; retain its alias or a compatible wrapper")),
   156	                Some(kind) if !accepts_in(old_kind,kind,Some(old),Some(new))=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: argument alias {alias} retyped or narrowed ({old_kind:?} → {kind:?}); retain its old input domain")),
   157	                _=>{}
   158	            }
   159	        }
   160	        let mut positions:BTreeMap<String,String>=BTreeMap::new();
   161	        for canonical in before.program.args.keys() {
   162	            for spelling in std::iter::once(canonical).chain(before.program.arg_aliases.iter().filter_map(|(alias,target)|(target==canonical).then_some(alias))) {
   163	                let target=after.program.args.contains_key(spelling).then_some(spelling).or_else(||after.program.arg_aliases.get(spelling));
   164	                if let Some(target)=target {
   165	                    if let Some(prior)=positions.insert(target.clone(),canonical.clone())&&prior!=*canonical {
   166	                        lines.push(format!("{prefix}: INPUT BREAK: independent arguments {prior} and {canonical} now share {target}; old calls containing both positions get E_INPUT; retain separate arguments or a compatible wrapper"));
   167	                    }
   168	                }
   169	            }
   170	        }
   171	        for (table,before_table) in old.schema.visible_tables() {
   172	            let Some(after_table)=new.schema.table(table) else { continue; };
   173	            if !snapback4_core::ir::read_sites(&before.program).iter().any(|site|site.table==*table)
   174	                && !snapback4_core::ir::write_tables(&before.program).iter().any(|(name,_)|name==table) { continue; }
   175	            for field in before_table.columns.keys().filter(|f|!before_table.read_optional(f)&&after_table.read_optional(f)) {
   176	                lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: {table}.{field} is now audience-optional; handle an omitted row property or a null explicit scalar before adopting the new column read rule"));
   177	            }
   178	        }
   179	        let action_change=action_result_change(old.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()),new.schema.action_specs.get(name).and_then(|s|s.returns.as_ref()));
   180	        let typed_change=result_change(&before.result,&after.result,old,new);
   181	        let change=combine([action_change,typed_change],false);
   182	        match change {
   183	            ResultChange::Additive=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT NOTE: result shape added fields while preserving prior fields and domains; old clients may ignore the additions")),
   184	            ResultChange::Changed=>lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: result shape/value domain changed; preserve the old projection/domain or introduce a new operation before retiring old clients")),
   185	            ResultChange::Same=>{},
   186	        }
   187	        let old_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(before,old);
   188	        let new_domains=crate::result_domains::signature(after,new);
   189	        // A domain introduced only for a newly returned field is covered by
   190	        // the additive result note. Existing or removed domains still need review.
   191	        let changed:Vec<_>=old_domains.keys().collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>().into_iter().filter(|key|old_domains.get(*key)!=new_domains.get(*key)).cloned().collect();
   192	        if !changed.is_empty() {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: RESULT REVIEW: declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: {}; results or refusals may change even when the TypeScript type stays number/string; preserve the old domains or verify old-client handling",changed.join(", ")));}
   193	        if refusals(before)!=refusals(after) {lines.push(format!("{prefix}: BEHAVIOR REVIEW: refusal codes/messages changed ({:?} → {:?}); verify intended denials separately from input breaks",refusals(before),refusals(after)));}
   194	    }
   195	    lines
   196	}
   197	
   198	/// Human result advice groups source columns across operations. JSON keeps compare().
   199	pub fn compact(lines:&[String])->Vec<String>{
   200	    use std::collections::BTreeSet;
   201	    let mut out=Vec::new();let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();
   202	    for line in lines {
   203	        let Some((prefix,detail))=line.split_once(": RESULT REVIEW: ") else {out.push(line.clone());continue};
   204	        let operation=prefix.rsplit_once("operation ").map(|(_,name)|name).unwrap_or("unknown");
   205	        if let Some((_,columns))=detail.split_once("declared source domains consumed by this operation changed: ") {
   206	            for column in columns.split(';').next().unwrap_or(columns).split(", "){groups.entry(column.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
   207	        }else{groups.entry(detail.into()).or_default().insert(operation.into());}
   208	    }
   209	    for(detail,ops)in groups{out.push(format!("old-client compatibility: RESULT REVIEW: {detail}; operations [{}]; verify old-client handling (full per-operation evidence in --json)",ops.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));}
   210	    out
   211	}

    70	                file.write_all(bytes).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    71	            }
    72	        }

    26	fn inspect(options: &Options) -> Result<()> {

    34	    let limit = match options.flags.get("limit") {
    35	        None => 200,
    36	        Some(value) => value.parse::<u32>().ok().filter(|n| *n > 0).ok_or(("E_INPUT", "--limit must be a positive 32-bit integer".into()))?,
    37	    };
    38	    let dormant = options.flags.contains_key("dormant");
    39	    let all_releases = options.flags.contains_key("all-releases");
    40	    if dormant && all_releases { return Err(("E_INPUT", "sql takes either --dormant or --all-releases, not both".into())); }
    41	    if (dormant || all_releases) && !options.flags.contains_key("release") {
    42	        return Err(("E_INPUT", "sql --dormant and --all-releases require an explicit --release <dir> deployment".into()));
    43	    }
    44	    let path = match options.flags.get("release") {
    45	        Some(dir) => Path::new(dir).join("store.sqlite"),
    46	        None => project_or_exit().store_path(),
    47	    };
    48	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — developer SQL is read-only, never rule-filtered
    49	    let conn = AnyInspection::open(&path).map_err(|error| {
    50	        let (code, message) = error;
    51	        (code, format!("{message}{}", store_hint(&path, options)))
    52	    })?;
    53	    conn.begin_snapshot()?;
    54	    // Catalog, compiled columns and rows all belong to the same WAL snapshot.
    55	    let (generation, active_schema) = catalog::active_schema(&conn)?;
    56	    let schema = if dormant || all_releases { conn.retained_schema(active_schema)? } else { active_schema };
    57	    let retained = conn.dormant_inventory()?;
    58	    let mode = if dormant { "dormant retained records" } else if all_releases { "active and retained records" } else { "active records" };
    59	    let header = format!("sql: developer's own store {} — {mode}; read-only, not rule-filtered", path.display());
    60	    if let Some(command) = command {
    61	        let result = catalog::inspect(&conn, &schema, command)?;
    62	        if options.json {
    63	            println!("{}", json!({ "header": header, "generation": generation, "tables": result, "ruleFiltered": false }));
    64	        } else {
    65	            eprintln!("{header}");
    66	            catalog::print(&result, generation);
    67	        }
    68	        if !dormant && !all_releases { dormant_notice(dormant_rows(&retained), "rerun SQL with --dormant and an explicit --release to inspect them"); }
    69	        return Ok(());
    70	    }
    71	    conn.build_retained_views(&schema, dormant, all_releases, |name| eprintln!("sql: skipping {name}: ephemeral rows live only in the serving process's memory"))?;
    72	    let object_rows = options.flags.contains_key("json-objects");
    73	    let snapback4_core::store_port::InspectionRows { columns, rows, more } = conn.query(&body, limit, object_rows,
    74	        |message| query_error(&schema, &retained, message),
    75	        |columns| snapback4_core::inspection::check_output_names(columns, object_rows),
    76	        |columns| objects::kinds(&body, &schema, columns, dormant || all_releases).map_err(|e| ("E_INPUT", e)))?;
    77	    if options.json {
    78	        let rows = if object_rows {
    79	            Value::Array(rows.into_iter().map(|values| Value::Object(columns.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect())).collect())
    80	        } else { json!(rows) };
    81	        println!("{}", json!({ "header": header, "columns": columns, "rows": rows, "limit": limit, "more": more, "ruleFiltered": false, "inspection": mode }));
    82	    } else {
    83	        eprintln!("{header}");
    84	        let cells: Vec<Vec<String>> = rows.iter().map(|row| row.iter().map(|v| match v { Value::String(s) => s.escape_debug().to_string(), _ => v.to_string() }).collect()).collect();
    85	        let widths: Vec<usize> = columns.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, name)| cells.iter().map(|row| row[i].chars().count()).chain([name.chars().count()]).max().unwrap()).collect();
    86	        let line = |cells: &[String]| cells.iter().zip(&widths).map(|(cell, width)| format!("{cell}{}", " ".repeat(width.saturating_sub(cell.chars().count())))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" | ");
    87	        println!("{}", line(&columns));
    88	        println!("{}", widths.iter().map(|n| "-".repeat(*n)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("-+-"));
    89	        for row in &cells { println!("{}", line(row)); }
    90	        eprintln!("{} row(s){}", rows.len(), if more { " — more rows exist; increase --limit or refine the SELECT" } else { "" });
    91	    }
    92	    if options.json && more { eprintln!("sql: result truncated at {limit} rows; increase --limit or refine the SELECT"); }
    93	    if !dormant && !all_releases { dormant_notice(dormant_rows(&retained), "rerun SQL with --dormant and an explicit --release to inspect them"); }
    94	    Ok(())
    95	}

    97	pub(super) fn dormant_rows(items: &[snapback4_core::release_history::DormantItem]) -> u64 {
    98	    items.iter().filter(|item| matches!(item.kind.as_str(), "table" | "rows")).map(|item| item.rows).sum()
    99	}
   100	
   101	pub(super) fn dormant_notice(rows: u64, advice: &str) {
   102	    if rows > 0 {
   103	        eprintln!("{rows} dormant {} retained; {advice}", if rows == 1 { "row" } else { "rows" });
   104	    }
   105	}
   106	
   107	pub(super) fn retained_table_rows(items: &[snapback4_core::release_history::DormantItem], table: &str) -> u64 {
   108	    items.iter().filter(|item| matches!(item.kind.as_str(), "table" | "rows") && item.path.eq_ignore_ascii_case(table)).map(|item| item.rows).sum()
   109	}

   111	fn query_error(schema: &Schema, retained: &[snapback4_core::release_history::DormantItem], message: String) -> (&'static str, String) {
   112	    let missing = message.strip_prefix("no such table: ").map(str::trim);
   113	    if let Some(table) = missing {
   114	        let rows = retained_table_rows(retained, table.trim_matches(['`', '"', '\'']));
   115	        if rows > 0 {
   116	            return ("E_INPUT", format!("SQL: {message}; {rows} retained dormant {} exist for {table}; inspect them with `snapback4 sql 'SELECT * FROM {table}' --release <dir> --dormant`", if rows == 1 { "row" } else { "rows" }));
   117	        }
   118	    }
   119	    snapback4_core::inspection::query_error(schema, message)
   120	}

   124	/// Population advice only for a newly declared/changed window, before adoption.
   125	// @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — bounded catalog probes never adopt or acquire a writer lock.
   126	pub(super) fn window_populations(path: &Path, candidate: &Schema) -> Result<Vec<(String, u32, u64)>> {
   127	    if !candidate.visible_tables().any(|(_, table)| table.ephemeral.is_none() && table.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.horizon.is_some())) { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
   128	    let conn = AnyInspection::open(path)?;
   129	    conn.begin_snapshot()?;
   130	    let adopted = conn.inspection_adopted()?;
   131	    if !adopted { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
   132	    let (_, active) = catalog::active_schema(&conn)?;
   133	    let mut populations = Vec::new();
   134	    for (name, table) in candidate.visible_tables() {
   135	        let Some(sync) = &table.sync else { continue; };
   136	        let Some(horizon) = &sync.horizon else { continue; };
   137	        let Some(previous) = active.tables.get(name) else { continue; };
   138	        if previous.sync == table.sync || table.ephemeral.is_some() { continue; }
   139	        let threshold = u64::from(horizon.last) * 10;
   140	        if threshold == 0 || threshold > catalog::COUNT_LIMIT { continue; }
   141	        let count = catalog::row_count(&conn, name, threshold)?;
   142	        if count == threshold { populations.push((name.clone(), horizon.last, count)); }
   143	    }
   144	    Ok(populations)
   145	}
