   147	/// Strip SQL comments without disturbing quotes, and permit a single trailing
   148	/// terminator. SQLite still parses and authorizes the actual statement.
   149	fn select_body(sql: &str) -> Result<String> {
   150	    if sql.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(PRIVATE) { return Err(("E_SQL_INTERNAL", format!("private inspection views cannot be named in SQL; {CATALOG_HINT}"))); }
   151	    let mut chars = sql.chars().peekable();
   152	    let mut body = String::new();
   153	    let mut ended = false;
   154	    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
   155	        if c == '-' && chars.peek() == Some(&'-') {
   156	            for c in chars.by_ref() { if c == '\n' { break; } }
   157	            body.push('\n');
   158	        } else if c == '/' && chars.peek() == Some(&'*') {
   159	            chars.next();
   160	            while let Some(c) = chars.next() { if c == '*' && chars.peek() == Some(&'/') { chars.next(); break; } }
   161	            body.push(' ');
   162	        } else if c.is_whitespace() { body.push(c); }
   163	        else if ended { return Err(("E_SQL_READ_ONLY", "sql accepts exactly one SELECT statement".into())); }
   164	        else if c == ';' { ended = true; }
   165	        else if matches!(c, '\'' | '"' | '`' | '[') {
   166	            let end = if c == '[' { ']' } else { c };
   167	            body.push(c);
   168	            while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
   169	                body.push(c);
   170	                if c == end {
   171	                    if end != ']' && chars.peek() == Some(&end) { body.push(chars.next().unwrap()); }
   172	                    else { break; }
   173	                }
   174	            }
   175	        } else { body.push(c); }
   176	    }
   177	    let first = body.trim_start().split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_alphabetic()).next().unwrap_or_default();
   178	    if !first.eq_ignore_ascii_case("select") && !first.eq_ignore_ascii_case("with") {
   179	        return Err(("E_SQL_READ_ONLY", "sql accepts one SELECT or WITH … SELECT statement".into()));
   180	    }
   181	    Ok(body)
   182	}
   183	
   184	// A quoted SQL string may itself contain a CLI-looking value. Only flag tokens
   185	// outside SQLite quotes are a misplaced option (including SQLite line comments).
   186	fn misplaced_flag(statement: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
   187	    let mut chars = statement.char_indices().peekable();
   188	    while let Some((offset, c)) = chars.next() {
   189	        if matches!(c, '\'' | '"' | '`' | '[') {
   190	            let end = if c == '[' { ']' } else { c };
   191	            while let Some((_, c)) = chars.next() {
   192	                if c == end {
   193	                    if end != ']' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == end) { chars.next(); }
   194	                    else { break; }
   195	                }
   196	            }
   197	        } else if c == '/' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == '*') {
   198	            chars.next();
   199	            while let Some((_, c)) = chars.next() {
   200	                if c == '*' && chars.peek().is_some_and(|(_, c)| *c == '/') { chars.next(); break; }
   201	            }
   202	        } else if c == '-' {
   203	            for flag in ["--release", "--dormant", "--all-releases", "--limit", "--json-objects", "--json"] {
   204	                if let Some(tail) = statement[offset..].strip_prefix(flag) {
   205	                    if tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(char::is_whitespace) || tail.starts_with('=') { return Some(flag); }
   206	                }
   207	            }
   208	        }
   209	    }
   210	    None
   211	}

   213	/// Missing development stores never imply that a neighbouring release is the
   214	/// store to inspect. Name the explicit selection without opening or adopting it.
   215	pub(super) fn store_hint(path: &Path, options: &Options) -> String {
   216	    if options.flags.contains_key("release") || path.exists() { return String::new(); }
   217	    let Some(root) = path.parent().and_then(Path::parent) else { return String::new(); };
   218	    let mut dirs = Vec::new();
   219	    if root.join("store.sqlite").is_file() { dirs.push(root.to_path_buf()); }
   220	    if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(root) {
   221	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
   222	            if entry.file_name() != ".snapback4" && entry.file_type().is_ok_and(|kind| kind.is_dir())
   223	                && entry.path().join("store.sqlite").is_file() { dirs.push(entry.path()); }
   224	        }
   225	    }
   226	    dirs.sort();
   227	    if dirs.is_empty() { return String::new(); }
   228	    format!("; no development store at {}. Deployment stores are present at {}; select one explicitly with --release <dir>",
   229	        path.display(), dirs.iter().map(|dir| dir.display().to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))
   230	}

     7	export function changelogFlags(changelog) {
     8	  // Changelog entries are newest first. The newest mention decides whether
     9	  // an option is supported; explicit retirement prose must not announce it.
    10	  const flags = new Map();
    11	  for (const line of changelog.split('\n')) {
    12	    let verb, packageManagerCommand = false;
    13	    const retired = [...line.matchAll(/\b(?:drops?|dropped|removes?|removed|retires?|retired)\s+(?:(?:the|unsupported)\s+)*[A-Za-z-]+\s+--[a-z][a-z-]*/gi)];

    15	    // Exact's rebuild command is an external tool, explicitly outside binary help.
    16	    for (const match of line.matchAll(/\b(?:exact\.mjs|[A-Za-z]+)\b|--[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/g)) {
    17	      const token = match[0];
    18	      if (['npm', 'bun', 'pnpm'].includes(token)) {
    19	        verb = 'package-manager';
    20	        packageManagerCommand = true;
    21	      }
    22	      else if (token === 'exact.mjs') verb = 'exact';
    23	      else if (verbs.has(token.toLowerCase())) {
    24	        // `run` immediately after npm/bun/pnpm names the package-manager
    25	        // subcommand. A later explicit Snapback verb still starts a new owner.
    26	        if (packageManagerCommand && token.toLowerCase() === 'run') packageManagerCommand = false;
    27	        else {
    28	          verb = token.toLowerCase();
    29	          packageManagerCommand = false;
    30	        }
    31	      }
    32	      else if (token.startsWith('--')) {
    33	        if (verb === 'package-manager' || verb === 'exact' && token === '--rebuild') continue;
    34	        if (!verb || verb === 'exact') throw new Error(`changelog flag ${token} needs an explicit Snapback verb: ${line}`);

    37	      }
    38	      else packageManagerCommand = false;
    39	    }
    40	  }
    41	  return [...flags.values()].filter(Boolean);
    42	}

    85	    return { ...host, personas: host.personas!, operatorToken, now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,

    90	      drain: (advanceOptions: Pick<AdvanceOptions,"eachBoundary"|"allowHeld"> = {}) => clockCall({duration:"0ms",drain:true,...advanceOptions}),
    91	    };
    92	  });

     1	//! SQLite erases booleans to integers. Recover direct column types from the
     2	//! adopted schema and SQL projection, never by guessing from names or 0/1.
     3	// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.26 — positional JSON stays compatible; boolean recovery is presentation on the operator's adopted snapshot.
     4	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — direct schema-proven media cells use their ordinary wire JSON in object rows.
     5	use snapback4_core::{inspection::InspectionColumnKind as Kind, schema::{ColumnType, Schema}};
     6	use sqlparser::{ast::{Expr, ObjectName, Query, SelectItem, SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind, SetExpr, Statement, TableFactor}, dialect::SQLiteDialect, parser::Parser};
     7	use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
     8	
     9	type Columns = Vec<(String, Kind)>;
    10	type Tables = BTreeMap<String, Columns>;
    11	
    12	pub(super) fn kinds(sql: &str, schema: &Schema, count: usize, retained: bool) -> Result<Vec<Kind>, String> {
    13	    let mut tables: Tables = schema.visible_tables().map(|(name, table)| {
    14	        let mut columns = vec![("id".into(), Kind::Plain)];
    15	        columns.extend(table.columns.iter().filter(|(name, _)| *name != "id")
    16	            .map(|(name, kind)| (name.to_ascii_lowercase(), if matches!(kind.required(), ColumnType::Bool) { Kind::Bool } else if kind.contains_asset() { Kind::Media } else { Kind::Plain })));
    17	        if retained {columns.extend([("_snapback_state".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_source".into(),Kind::Plain),("_snapback_columns".into(),Kind::Plain)]);}
    18	        (name.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns)
    19	    }).collect();
    20	    let statements = Parser::parse_sql(&SQLiteDialect {}, sql).map_err(|e| format!("--json-objects SQL projection: {e}; use --json for SQLite-specific syntax"))?;
    21	    let [Statement::Query(query)] = statements.as_slice() else { return Err("--json-objects takes a SELECT".into()); };
    22	    let columns = query_columns(query, &mut tables)?;
    23	    if columns.len() != count { return Err("--json-objects cannot determine this projection's column types; select explicit columns or use --json".into()); }
    24	    Ok(columns.into_iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind).collect())
    25	}
    26	
    27	fn name(name: &ObjectName) -> Option<String> {
    28	    // SQLite schema qualification bypasses CTE shadowing; do not erase it.
    29	    if name.0.len() != 1 { return None; }
    30	    name.0.last()?.as_ident().map(|id| id.value.to_ascii_lowercase())
    31	}
    32	
    33	fn query_columns(query: &Query, inherited: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    34	    let mut tables = inherited.clone();
    35	    if let Some(with) = &query.with {
    36	        if with.recursive { return Err("--json-objects does not infer recursive CTE types; use --json".into()); }
    37	        for cte in &with.cte_tables {
    38	            if tables.contains_key(&cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
    39	                return Err("--json-objects does not infer shadowing CTEs; use --json".into());
    40	            }
    41	            let mut columns = query_columns(&cte.query, &mut tables)?;
    42	            for (column, alias) in columns.iter_mut().zip(&cte.alias.columns) { column.0 = alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(); }
    43	            tables.insert(cte.alias.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), columns);
    44	        }
    45	    }
    46	    set_columns(&query.body, &mut tables)
    47	}
    48	
    49	fn relation(factor: &TableFactor, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<(String, Columns), String> {
    50	    match factor {
    51	        TableFactor::Table { name: object, alias, args: None, .. } => {
    52	            let key = name(object).ok_or("--json-objects does not infer schema-qualified relations; use --json")?;
    53	            let columns = tables.get(&key).ok_or("--json-objects needs application tables or typed CTEs")?.clone();
    54	            Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or(key), columns))
    55	        }
    56	        TableFactor::Derived { subquery, alias, .. } => Ok((alias.as_ref().map(|a| a.name.value.to_ascii_lowercase()).unwrap_or_default(), query_columns(subquery, tables)?)),
    57	        _ => Err("--json-objects cannot infer this table expression; use --json".into()),
    58	    }
    59	}
    60	
    61	fn set_columns(body: &SetExpr, tables: &mut Tables) -> Result<Columns, String> {
    62	    match body {
    63	        SetExpr::Query(q) => query_columns(q, tables),
    64	        SetExpr::SetOperation { left, right, .. } => {
    65	            let mut left = set_columns(left, tables)?;
    66	            let right = set_columns(right, tables)?;
    67	            if left.len() != right.len() { return Err("incompatible SQL projections".into()); }
    68	            for (l, r) in left.iter_mut().zip(right) { if l.1 != r.1 { l.1 = Kind::Plain; } }
    69	            Ok(left)
    70	        }
    71	        SetExpr::Select(select) => {
    72	            let mut sources = Vec::new();
    73	            for from in &select.from {
    74	                sources.push(relation(&from.relation, tables)?);
    75	                for join in &from.joins { sources.push(relation(&join.relation, tables)?); }
    76	            }
    77	            let mut output = Vec::new();
    78	            for item in &select.projection {
    79	                match item {
    80	                    SelectItem::Wildcard(_) => output.extend(sources.iter().flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.clone())),
    81	                    SelectItem::QualifiedWildcard(SelectItemQualifiedWildcardKind::ObjectName(object), _) => {
    82	                        let key = name(object).ok_or("unsupported wildcard")?;
    83	                        let (_, cols) = sources.iter().find(|(alias, _)| *alias == key).ok_or("unknown wildcard table")?;
    84	                        output.extend(cols.clone());
    85	                    }
    86	                    SelectItem::UnnamedExpr(expr) => {
    87	                        let mut direct = expr;
    88	                        while let Expr::Nested(inner) = direct { direct = inner; }
    89	                        let label = match direct {
    90	                            Expr::Identifier(id) => id.value.clone(),
    91	                            Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) => ids.last().unwrap().value.clone(),
    92	                            _ => expr.to_string(),
    93	                        };
    94	                        output.push((label.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources)));
    95	                    }
    96	                    SelectItem::ExprWithAlias { expr, alias } => output.push((alias.value.to_ascii_lowercase(), kind(expr, &sources))),
    97	                    _ => return Err("unsupported object-row projection; use --json".into()),
    98	                }
    99	            }
   100	            let mut names = BTreeSet::new();
   101	            if output.iter().any(|(name, _)| !names.insert(name)) {
   102	                return Err("--json-objects needs unique names in every projection; alias duplicate columns".into());
   103	            }
   104	            Ok(output)
   105	        }
   106	        _ => Err("--json-objects needs a SELECT projection; use --json".into()),
   107	    }
   108	}
   109	
   110	fn kind(expr: &Expr, sources: &[(String, Columns)]) -> Kind {
   111	    let (table, column) = match expr {
   112	        Expr::Nested(expr) => return kind(expr, sources),
   113	        Expr::Identifier(id) => (None, &id.value),
   114	        Expr::CompoundIdentifier(ids) if ids.len() == 2 => (Some(ids[0].value.to_ascii_lowercase()), &ids[1].value),
   115	        _ => return Kind::Plain, // Computed SQL expressions retain SQLite's own types.
   116	    };
   117	    let found: Vec<Kind> = sources.iter().filter(|(alias, _)| table.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t == alias))
   118	        .flat_map(|(_, cols)| cols.iter().filter(|(name, _)| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(column)).map(|(_, kind)| *kind)).collect();
   119	    // An unqualified duplicate only reaches execution when SQLite resolved it
   120	    // through USING/NATURAL. All contributors must agree before typing it bool.
   121	    found.first().copied().filter(|first| found.iter().all(|kind| kind == first)).unwrap_or(Kind::Plain)
   122	}

   338	/** Match the smallest visible element whose composed descendant text matches.
   339	 * Strings normalize whitespace and stay exact by default; regexes keep their
   340	 * own semantics. Editable values never count. Independent matches remain

   344	export function renderedText(page: Page, text: string | RegExp, options: { within?: Locator; exact?: boolean } | null = {}): Locator {

   349	    flags: typeof text === "string" ? "" : text.flags,

   357	export interface ExhaustPagesOptions {
   358	  /** Refuse rather than loop forever when a backend returns bad continuations. */
   359	  maxPages?: number;
   360	  /** Names the read in a refusal without exposing its rows or cursor. */
   361	  label?: string;

   363	type ProofPage<Row> =
   364	  | { readonly data: readonly Row[]; readonly next?: Cursor | null; readonly complete: boolean; readonly cut: ReadCut; readonly existence?: "present" | "absent" | "partial" }
   365	  | { readonly denied: Refusal }
   366	  | { readonly loading: true };
   367	/** Read every page by passing each opaque `next` back unchanged. The callback
   368	 * receives null first. Refusals, loading, malformed/repeated cursors and a
   369	 * capped or incomplete page fail instead of returning a partial snapshot. */
   370	/** @throws E_PROOF_PAGE for a refused, loading, malformed, repeated, incomplete or over-limit traversal; callback errors propagate. */
   371	// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#10-wave-25-day-two-friction-dx8 — proof traversal must never promote capped or partial reads to complete evidence.
   372	export async function exhaustPages<Row>(readPage: (cursor: Cursor | null) => Promise<ProofPage<Row>>, options: ExhaustPagesOptions = {}): Promise<Row[]> {
   373	  const maxPages = options.maxPages ?? 1_000, label = options.label ?? "paged read";
   374	  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(maxPages) || maxPages < 1) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: maxPages must be a positive safe integer`);
   375	  const rows: Row[] = [], seen = new Set<string>();
   376	  let cursor: Cursor | null = null;
   377	  for (let pageNumber = 1; pageNumber <= maxPages; pageNumber++) {
   378	    const page = await readPage(cursor);
   379	    if (!page || typeof page !== "object") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned no read envelope`);
   380	    if ("denied" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} refused ${page.denied.code}: ${page.denied.message}`);
   381	    if ("loading" in page) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is still loading`);
   382	    if (!Array.isArray(page.data)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} data is not an array`);
   383	    if (page.cut !== null) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (${page.cut === undefined ? "missing" : page.cut} cut)`);
   384	    if (page.complete !== true) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} is incomplete (complete must be true)`);
   385	    if (page.existence === "partial") throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} has partial existence`);
   386	    rows.push(...page.data);
   387	    const next = page.next ?? null;
   388	    if (next === null) return rows;
   389	    if (typeof next !== "string" || next.length === 0) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a malformed cursor`);
   390	    if (seen.has(next)) throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: page ${pageNumber} returned a repeated cursor`);
   391	    seen.add(next);
   392	    cursor = next as Cursor;
   393	  }
   394	  throw new Error(`E_PROOF_PAGE: ${label}: exceeded maxPages ${maxPages}`);
   395	}

    43	/// Shared schema-first ordering retains saved modules' original namespaces.
    44	pub(crate) fn sources(path: &std::path::Path) -> io::Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {
    45	    if !path.try_exists()? {return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound,format!("{}: not saved yet: saved source does not exist",path.display())));}
    46	    let bad = |message: &str| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, message);
    47	    let mut paths = if path.is_dir() {
    48	        std::fs::read_dir(path)?.map(|entry| entry.map(|entry| entry.path())).collect::<io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?
    49	            .into_iter().filter(|path| path.is_file() && path.extension().is_some_and(|extension| extension == "q")).collect::<Vec<_>>()

//! Table names may change; numeric row, reference and receipt lifetimes do not.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#8-wave-21-release-evolution — renames are identity moves, never row copies or merges.
use super::*;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
pub(super) const VERSION:&str="snapback4-release-store-10";
fn refuse(s:impl Into<String>)->RuntimeError {RuntimeError::Structural{code:"E_ADOPT",message:s.into()}}

// Only structural table identifiers change. Literal values, column names,
// operation names and authored defaults are never table identifiers.
fn identifiers(value:&mut serde_json::Value,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>) {
    match value {
        serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs {identifiers(x,map)},
        serde_json::Value::Object(fields)=>for (key,x) in fields {
            if key=="Literal" || key=="defaults" {continue;}
            if matches!(key.as_str(),"table"|"parent") {if let Some(name)=x.as_str().and_then(|s|map.get(s)){*x=serde_json::Value::String(name.clone());continue;}}
            identifiers(x,map);
        },_=>()
    }
}
fn mapped(name:&str,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->String {map.get(name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(||name.into())}
fn remap<T:serde::Serialize+serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(value:&T,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->Result<T,RuntimeError> {
    let mut json=serde_json::to_value(value).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;identifiers(&mut json,map);
    serde_json::from_value(json).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))
}
pub(crate) fn schema(mut schema:Schema,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->Result<Schema,RuntimeError> {
    if map.is_empty(){return Ok(schema)}
    schema.tables=std::mem::take(&mut schema.tables).into_iter().map(|(name,table)|Ok((mapped(&name,map),remap(&table,map)?))).collect::<Result<_,RuntimeError>>()?;
    for m in &mut schema.maintains {*m=remap(m,map)?;m.source=mapped(&m.source,map);m.target=mapped(&m.target,map);}
    for f in &mut schema.backfills {fill(f,map,false)?;}
    for f in &mut schema.downfills {fill(f,map,true)?;}
    for e in &mut schema.extractions {e.child=mapped(&e.child,map);}
    // Remaining table-bearing structural metadata is normalized through the
    // same typed codec; maintains' source/target are handled explicitly above.
    // These maps contain column identifiers, including arbitrary keys such as
    // "parent". Normalize their typed table slots, never their column strings.
    let mut extractions=std::mem::take(&mut schema.extractions);
    for e in &mut extractions {e.parent=mapped(&e.parent,map);}
    let columns=std::mem::take(&mut schema.asset_renames).into_iter().map(|(name,columns)|(mapped(&name,map),columns)).collect();
    schema.table_renames.clear();schema=remap(&schema,map)?;
    schema.extractions=extractions;schema.asset_renames=columns;
    Ok(schema)
}
fn fill(f:&mut crate::schema::backfill::Backfill,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>,down:bool)->Result<(),RuntimeError> {
    *f=remap(f,map)?;
    f.program.name=format!("{}{}{}",if down{"down"}else{"backfill"},f.table,f.name);Ok(())
}
pub(super) fn prepare(conn:&Connection,next:&Schema,catalog:&mut BTreeMap<String,i64>)->Result<BTreeMap<String,String>,RuntimeError> {
    let exists:bool=conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='_table_renames')",[],|r|r.get(0))?;
    if !exists && next.table_renames.is_empty(){return Ok(BTreeMap::new())}
    conn.execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _table_renames(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY,origin TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;")?;
    let mut names:BTreeMap<String,String>=conn.prepare("SELECT name,origin FROM _table_renames")?.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
    for (new,old) in &next.table_renames {
        if new==old || !next.tables.contains_key(new) || next.tables.contains_key(old){return Err(refuse("table rename requires a distinct predecessor-only source"))}
        let origin=names.get(old).cloned().unwrap_or_else(||old.clone());
        if names.get(new).is_some_and(|root|root!=&origin){return Err(refuse(format!("table rename {old} → {new} conflicts with an independent retained identity")))}
        if let (Some(a),Some(b))=(catalog.get(old),catalog.get(new)) {if a!=b{return Err(refuse(format!("table rename {old} → {new} cannot merge existing table lifetimes")))}}
        for name in [old,new] {names.insert(name.clone(),origin.clone());conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _table_renames VALUES(?1,?2)",params![name,origin])?;}
    }
    let mut selected=BTreeMap::<String,String>::new();
    for name in next.tables.keys() {if let Some(root)=names.get(name) {if let Some(other)=selected.insert(root.clone(),name.clone()){return Err(refuse(format!("table aliases {other} and {name} cannot be active together")))}}}
    let map:BTreeMap<String,String>=names.iter().filter_map(|(name,root)|selected.get(root).filter(|new|*new!=name).map(|new|(name.clone(),new.clone()))).collect();
    for (old,new) in &map {
        if !catalog.contains_key(old){continue;}
        if catalog.contains_key(new){return Err(refuse(format!("table rename {old} → {new} conflicts with retained table storage")))}
        let entries:Vec<_>=catalog.iter().filter(|(key,_)|*key==old || key.starts_with(&format!("{old}."))).map(|(k,v)|(k.clone(),*v)).collect();
        for (key,num) in entries {let renamed=format!("{new}{}",&key[old.len()..]);conn.execute("UPDATE _catalog SET name=?1 WHERE name=?2",params![renamed,key])?;catalog.remove(&key);catalog.insert(renamed,num);}
        conn.execute("UPDATE _assets SET home_table=?1 WHERE home_table=?2",params![new,old])?;
        for table in ["_dormant_tables","_dormant_columns","_dormant_indexes"] {
            if conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name=?1)",[table],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))? {conn.execute(&format!("UPDATE {table} SET table_name=?1 WHERE table_name=?2"),params![new,old])?;}
        }
    }
    // Retained typed definitions must use the current public table names too.
    for table in ["_dormant_tables","_dormant_columns","_dormant_narrow_rows"] {
        if !conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name=?1)",[table],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))? {continue;}
        let rows:Vec<(String,String)>=conn.prepare(&format!("SELECT definition,definition FROM {table} GROUP BY definition"))?.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
        for (old,text) in rows {let mut json:serde_json::Value=serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;identifiers(&mut json,&map);let new=canonical_json(&json);if old!=new {conn.execute(&format!("UPDATE {table} SET definition=?1 WHERE definition=?2"),params![new,old])?;}}
    }
    history(conn,&map)?;
    conn.execute("UPDATE _meta SET value=?1 WHERE key='version'",[VERSION])?;
    Ok(map)
}
fn history(conn:&Connection,map:&BTreeMap<String,String>)->Result<(),RuntimeError> {
    for (table,down) in [("_backfill_definitions",false),("_downfill_definitions",true)] {
        if !conn.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name=?1)",[table],|r|r.get::<_,bool>(0))? {continue;}
        let rows:Vec<(String,String)>=conn.prepare(&format!("SELECT digest,definition FROM {table}"))?.query_map([],|r|Ok((r.get(0)?,r.get(1)?)))?.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?;
        for (old,text) in rows {let mut f:crate::schema::backfill::Backfill=serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;fill(&mut f,map,down)?;let new=if down {f.down_key()}else{f.key()};if old==new{continue;}
            conn.execute(&format!("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO {table} VALUES(?1,?2)"),params![new,canonical_json(&f)])?;
            for ledger in ["_backfill_evidence","_backfill_pruned","_backfill_absence"] {conn.execute(&format!("UPDATE {ledger} SET definition=?1 WHERE definition=?2"),params![new,old])?;}
            conn.execute("UPDATE _backfill_absence SET definition=?1 WHERE definition=?2",params![format!("$native:{new}"),format!("$native:{old}")])?;
            conn.execute("UPDATE _backfill_absence SET definition=?1 WHERE definition=?2",params![format!("$authored:{new}"),format!("$authored:{old}")])?;
            for c in f.inputs.keys() {conn.execute("UPDATE _dormant_refs SET column_name=?1 WHERE column_name=?2",params![format!("$backfill:{new}:{c}"),format!("$backfill:{old}:{c}")])?;}
            conn.execute(&format!("DELETE FROM {table} WHERE digest=?1"),[old])?;
        }
    }Ok(())
}

 succeeded in 0ms:
//! Conservative source-domain evidence for operation results and refusal behavior.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000#11-old-client-operation-contracts-rel5 — TypeScript numbers/strings must not erase consumed source-domain changes.
use crate::{Bound,BoundProgram};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap,BTreeSet};

// Inspect the complete operation: result construction may flow through writes,
// loops, merges, helper blocks or aggregate selectors. This deliberately includes
// guard/order dependencies rather than claiming a partial lineage analysis is exact.
fn consumed(value:&Value,tables:&mut BTreeSet<String>,fields:&mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    match value {
        Value::Object(object)=> {
            // Read, scan, merge lane, recursion and write targets all carry table.
            if let Some(table)=object.get("table").and_then(Value::as_str) {tables.insert(table.into());}
            if let Some(field)=object.get("Field") && let Some(name)=field["name"].as_str() {fields.insert(name.into());}
            // Aggregate, optional-field, range and sort selectors carry field directly.
            for key in ["field","next_field"] {if let Some(field)=object.get(key).and_then(Value::as_str) {fields.insert(field.into());}}
            for child in object.values() {consumed(child,tables,fields);}
        }
        Value::Array(array)=>for child in array {consumed(child,tables,fields);},
        _=>{}
    }
}
type Definitions=BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>;
fn definitions(value:&Value,defs:&mut Definitions) {
    match value {
        Value::Object(object)=> {
            for kind in ["Let","Const","Assign"] {
                if let Some(binding)=object.get(kind) && let Some(name)=binding["name"].as_str() {defs.entry(name.into()).or_default().push(binding["value"].clone());}
            }
            for child in object.values(){definitions(child,defs);}
        }
        Value::Array(array)=>for child in array{definitions(child,defs);},
        _=>{}
    }
}
fn payload_keys(value:&Value,defs:&Definitions,seen:&mut BTreeSet<String>)->Option<BTreeSet<String>> {
    if let Some(object)=value.get("Object").and_then(Value::as_object) {return Some(object.keys().cloned().collect());}
    if let Some(name)=value.get("Variable").and_then(Value::as_str) {
        if !seen.insert(name.into()){return None;}
        let mut keys=BTreeSet::new();
        for value in defs.get(name)? {keys.extend(payload_keys(value,defs,&mut seen.clone())?);}
        return Some(keys);
    }
    if let Some(shape)=value.get("Shape") {
        let mut keys=payload_keys(&shape["base"],defs,seen)?;
        keys.extend(shape["fields"].as_object()?.keys().cloned());return Some(keys);
    }
    if let Some(block)=value.get("Block") {return payload_keys(&block["value"],defs,seen);}
    None
}
fn writes(value:&Value,defs:&Definitions,bound:&Bound,fields:&mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    match value {
        Value::Object(object)=> {
            for (kind,payload) in [("Insert","row"),("InsertIfAbsent","row"),("Upsert","row"),("Update","patch"),("WriteTarget","patch")] {
                if let Some(write)=object.get(kind) {
                    if let Some(keys)=payload_keys(&write[payload],defs,&mut BTreeSet::new()) {fields.extend(keys);}
                    else {
                        // Opaque/spread write images conservatively consume their target domain.
                        let table=if kind=="WriteTarget" {write["target"]["table"].as_str()} else {write["table"].as_str()};
                        if let Some(table)=table.and_then(|name|bound.schema.table(name)) {fields.extend(table.columns.keys().cloned());}
                    }
                }
            }
            for child in object.values(){writes(child,defs,bound,fields);}
        }
        Value::Array(array)=>for child in array{writes(child,defs,bound,fields);},
        _=>{}
    }
}
fn row_fields(ty:&crate::types::Ty,bound:&Bound,fields:&mut BTreeSet<String>) {
    use crate::types::Ty;
    match ty {
        Ty::Row(name)|Ty::WriteRow(name)|Ty::Page(name,_)=>if let Some(table)=bound.schema.table(name) {fields.extend(table.columns.keys().cloned());},
        Ty::RowShape(parts)|Ty::RowObject(parts)=>{fields.extend(parts.keys().cloned());for ty in parts.values(){row_fields(ty,bound,fields);}},
        Ty::Object(parts)=>for ty in parts.values(){row_fields(ty,bound,fields);},
        Ty::Optional(ty)|Ty::Omittable(ty)|Ty::List(ty,_)|Ty::Collection(ty,_)=>row_fields(ty,bound,fields),
        _=>{}
    }
}
pub(crate) fn signature(program:&BoundProgram,bound:&Bound)->BTreeMap<String,String> {
    let mut tables=BTreeSet::new();let mut fields=BTreeSet::new();
    let body=serde_json::to_value(&program.program.body).unwrap();
    consumed(&body,&mut tables,&mut fields);
    let mut defs=Definitions::new();definitions(&body,&mut defs);writes(&body,&defs,bound,&mut fields);
    for read in snapback4_core::ir::read_sites(&program.program) {
        if let Some(table)=bound.schema.table(&read.table) && let Some(index)=table.index(&read.index) {
            // Physical key labels omit word/calendar/contribution source columns.
            fields.extend(table.columns.keys().filter(|column|index.uses_column(column)).cloned());
        }
    }
    row_fields(&program.result,bound,&mut fields);
    let mut out=BTreeMap::new();
    for name in tables {
        let Some(table)=bound.schema.table(&name) else {continue;};
        for field in &fields {
            if let Some(kind)=table.columns.get(field) {
                let constraints:Vec<_>=table.constraints.iter().filter(|c|matches!(c,snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Text{field:name,..} if name==field)).collect();
                out.insert(format!("{name}.{field}"),format!("{kind:?};{constraints:?}"));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

    16	/// The address `doctor` dials for the server that owns this store: the
    17	/// published loopback address itself, or, for a wildcard bind, that family's

    19	pub(crate) fn inspector_address(store: &Path) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {

    24	fn dialable(published: &str) -> Option<std::net::SocketAddr> {
    25	    use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr, Ipv6Addr, SocketAddr};
    26	    let address = published.strip_prefix("http://")?.parse::<SocketAddr>().ok()?;
    27	    let ip = match address.ip() {
    28	        ip if ip.is_loopback() => ip,
    29	        IpAddr::V4(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST),
    30	        IpAddr::V6(ip) if ip.is_unspecified() => IpAddr::V6(Ipv6Addr::LOCALHOST),
    31	        _ => return None,
    32	    };
    33	    (address.port() != 0).then(|| SocketAddr::new(ip, address.port()))
    34	}

    36	fn resolve(store: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    37	    match store.canonicalize() {
    38	        Ok(path) => Ok(path),
    39	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    40	            let parent = store.parent().filter(|p| !p.as_os_str().is_empty()).unwrap_or(Path::new("."));
    41	            snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(parent).map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?;
    42	            Ok(parent.canonicalize().map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?.join(store.file_name().ok_or("store path has no filename")?))
    43	        }
    44	        Err(e) => Err(failure(store, e)),
    45	    }
    46	}

    77	/// Read-only release barrier: never initializes SQLite, creates a lock file,
    78	/// clears an address, or treats a PID/listener hint as authority.
    79	#[cfg(unix)]
    80	pub(crate) fn wait_released(store: &Path, wait: Duration) -> Result<(), String> {
    81	    let path = store.canonicalize().map_err(|e| failure(store, e))?;
    82	    let before = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path,e))?
    83	        .ok_or_else(|| failure(&path,"store disappeared"))?;
    84	    let sidecar = match snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(&path, &snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&path), false, 0) {
    85	        Ok(file) => file,
    86	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(()),
    87	        Err(e) => return Err(failure(&path,e)),
    88	    };
    89	    let end = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
    90	    loop {
    91	        match sidecar.try_lock() {
    92	            Ok(()) => break,
    93	            Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now() < end => std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)),
    94	            Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return Err(busy(&path)),
    95	            Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(e)) => return Err(failure(&path,e)),
    96	        }
    97	    }
    98	    let after = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e|failure(&path,e))?;
    99	    if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&path,&sidecar) || !after.is_some_and(|after|same_file(&before,&after)) {
   100	        return Err(failure(&path,"store or ownership sidecar changed while waiting"));
   101	    }
   102	    Ok(())
   103	}

   108	#[cfg(unix)]
   109	fn acquire(store: &Path, shared: bool, wait: Duration, cleanup_only: bool) -> Result<Owner, String> {
   110	    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + wait;
   111	    for _ in 0..16 {
   112	        let path = resolve(store)?;
   113	        snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(path.parent().ok_or("store path has no parent")?)
   114	            .map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
   115	        // Stat before opening either auxiliary file; a refused probe creates
   116	        // no database. Only the sidecar lock grants permission to create one.
   117	        let before = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
   118	        let sidecar = snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_file(&path)
   119	            .map_err(|e| failure(&snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&path), e))?;
   120	        let mut cleanup = None;
   121	        loop {
   122	            let locked = if shared { sidecar.try_lock_shared() } else { sidecar.try_lock() };
   123	            match locked {
   124	                Ok(()) => break,
   125	                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now() < deadline && (!cleanup_only || *cleanup.get_or_insert_with(|| stopped_host(&path))) => {
   126	                    if cleanup.is_none() { eprintln!("waiting for store owner cleanup: {} (up to {} ms); no work admitted", path.display(), wait.as_millis()); cleanup = Some(true); }
   127	                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25));
   128	                },
   129	                Err(fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => return Err(busy(&path)),
   130	                Err(fs::TryLockError::Error(error)) => return Err(failure(&path, error)),
   131	            }
   132	        }
   133	        if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&path, &sidecar) { continue; }
   134	        snapback4_core::private_fs::database_file(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?;
   135	        let database = snapback4_core::private_fs::database_metadata(&path).map_err(|e| failure(&path, e))?
   136	            .ok_or_else(|| failure(&path, "database disappeared during ownership acquisition"))?;
   137	        if before.as_ref().is_some_and(|old| !same_file(old, &database)) { continue; }
   138	        let mut reclaimed = None;
   139	        let record = if shared { None } else {
   140	            let record_path = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
   141	            if let Some(pid)=owner_pid(&path) {
   142	                if unsafe {libc::kill(pid as libc::pid_t,0)} == -1 && std::io::Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error()==Some(libc::ESRCH) {
   143	                    reclaimed = Some(format!("reclaimed stale serve.lock: dead PID {pid}; directory {}", path.parent().unwrap().display()));
   144	                }
   145	            }
   146	            let file = regular(&record_path, true, &path)?;
   147	            file.set_len(0).map_err(|e| failure(&record_path, e))?;
   148	            Some(file)
   149	        };
   150	        return Ok(Owner { _sidecar: std::sync::Arc::new(sidecar), identity: (database.dev(), database.ino()), path, record, reclaimed, token_authority: None });
   151	    }
   152	    Err(failure(store, "database path kept changing during ownership acquisition"))
   153	}

   158	pub(crate) fn stopped_host(path: &Path) -> bool {
   159	    // A CLI owner or a host not yet announced still refuses immediately. A
   160	    // reachable listener does too; only a prior host's cleanup gets a wait.
   161	    // This is a refusal/wait hint, never permission to open the store: the
   162	    // sidecar must still be acquired. Never dial a non-loopback address hint.
   163	    address(path).is_some_and(|published| dialable(&published).is_none_or(|address|
   164	        std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, Duration::from_millis(50)).is_err()))
   165	}
   166	
   167	pub(crate) fn busy(path: &Path) -> String {
   168	    let owner = address(path).map(|address| match owner_pid(path) { Some(pid) => format!("{address} (pid {pid})"), None => address })
   169	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "another CLI command or a server starting up (address pending)".into());
   170	    format!("E_STORE_BUSY at {}: this store is live; owned by {owner}; directory {}; no work was admitted. For a disposable parallel proof use `dev --memory` (startDev({{args:[\"--memory\"]}})); otherwise stop its `snapback4 dev` or `snapback4 serve` process (or wait for the owning CLI command), rerun this command once, then restart the server. Exclusion holds while <database>-owner is left in place; deleting or replacing it while a process runs ends exclusion and does not stop that process", path.display(),path.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(".")).display())
   171	}

   173	#[cfg(unix)]
   174	pub(crate) fn address(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
   175	    // A missing/replaced address record cannot grant ownership. Never follow
   176	    // a symlink (including one to the database), nor block on a FIFO.
   177	    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
   178	    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
   179	    let mut text = String::new();
   180	    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
   181	    let mut lines = text.lines();
   182	    let port = lines.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok());
   183	    lines.next().map(str::to_owned).or_else(|| port.map(|p| format!("http://127.0.0.1:{p}")))
   184	}
   185	
   186	/// The owning host's PID from its address record (`pid N` on the third line).
   187	#[cfg(unix)]
   188	fn owner_pid(path: &Path) -> Option<u32> {
   189	    let record = path.with_file_name("serve.lock");
   190	    let file = regular(&record, false, path).ok()?;
   191	    let mut text = String::new();
   192	    file.take(1024).read_to_string(&mut text).ok()?;
   193	    text.lines().nth(2)?.strip_prefix("pid ")?.parse().ok()
   194	}

     1	//! Preflight activation pages before owning their serialized row images.
     2	use super::*;
     3	use crate::{error::MeterKind, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{adoption, word_heap as heap}};
     4	
     5	pub(super) fn walk(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
     6	    walk_metered(tx, table, adoption::Work::DECODE, None, |id, row, _| visit(id, row))
     7	}
     8	
     9	// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.24.1 — reserve stored bytes before fetching or decoding; page scratch stays live until consumed.
    10	pub(super) fn walk_metered(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> crate::value::InternalPrice>,
    11	    visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    12	    let checked=|row:&Value|Ok(scratch.map_or_else(crate::value::InternalPrice::zero,|f|f(row)));
    13	    walk_metered_checked(tx,table,work,scratch.map(|_|&checked as &dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>),visit)
    14	}
    15	
    16	/// Row-specific provenance can fail closed before any page callback runs.
    17	pub(super) fn walk_metered_checked(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: i64, work: adoption::Work,
    18	    scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<crate::value::InternalPrice,RuntimeError>>,
    19	    mut visit: impl FnMut(&str, Value, &mut Meter) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    20	    const PAGE: usize = 256;
    21	    let mut after: Option<String> = None;
    22	    loop {
    23	        // One job meter per page, shared with contribution evaluation. Retain
    24	        // the continuation's allowance across the page; reset only after all
    25	        // its row images and callback scratch have been consumed and dropped.
    26	        let mut meter = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
    27	        meter.at("adopt stored rows");
    28	        meter.heap(after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
    29	        meter.once(crate::meter::HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 2 * tx.page_size)?;
    30	        let page_mark = meter.mark();
    31	        let mut limit = PAGE;
    32	        let mut page = loop {
    33	            limit = work.limit(&meter, limit);
    34	            let sizes = if after.is_some() {
    35	                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
    36	            } else {
    37	                "SELECT octet_length(id), octet_length(data) FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
    38	            };
    39	            let (mut count, mut bytes) = (0, 0u64);
    40	            {
    41	                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(sizes)?;
    42	                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, limit as i64])?;
    43	                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
    44	                    let id_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize;
    45	                    let data_bytes = row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize;
    46	                    // Rust-owned text, two native payload copies, allocation
    47	                    // headers and exact Vec slots. Length preflight borrows no
    48	                    // overflow payload (the same SQLite convention as scans).
    49	                    let next = bytes.saturating_add(3 * (heap::allocation(id_bytes) + heap::allocation(data_bytes)) + 64 + heap::slots::<(String, String)>(1));
    50	                    // This first size estimate bounds the fetch; admission below
    51	                    // also checks the actual decoder and contribution allowance.
    52	                    if count > 0 && next > meter.ceilings.heap_bytes / 2 { break; }
    53	                    meter.heap(next - bytes)?;
    54	                    bytes = next;
    55	                    count += 1;
    56	                }
    57	            }
    58	            if count == 0 { return Ok(()); }
    59	            let query = if after.is_some() {
    60	                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id > ?2 ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
    61	            } else {
    62	                "SELECT id, data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND ?2 IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT ?3"
    63	            };
    64	            let mut page = Vec::<(String, String)>::with_capacity(count);
    65	            {
    66	                let mut statement = tx.tx.prepare_cached(query)?;
    67	                let mut rows = statement.query(params![table, after, count as i64])?;
    68	                while let Some(row) = rows.next()? { page.push((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)); }
    69	            }
    70	            if adoption::page_fits_checked(page.iter().map(|(_, data)| data.as_str()), &mut meter, work, scratch)? { break page; }
    71	            limit = (page.len() / 2).max(1);
    72	            drop(page);
    73	            meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
    74	        };
    75	        for (id, data) in &page {
    76	            let row_mark = meter.mark();
    77	            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
    78	            // Decode plus copy-on-write projection, optional materialization
    79	            // and validation scratch. Contribution keys reserve more through
    80	            // this same meter, on top of the still-resident complete page.
    81	            adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
    82	            let row = serde_json::from_str(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
    83	            visit(id, row, &mut meter)?;
    84	            meter.release_heap(row_mark);
    85	        }
    86	        // Move the last ID into the next page's continuation, without an
    87	        // unpriced clone. Drop every other fetched byte before releasing.
    88	        after = page.pop().map(|row| row.0);
    89	        drop(page);
    90	        meter.release_heap(page_mark);
    91	    }
    92	}

//! Admission for a fetched adoption page, before any callback can write.
use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::Meter, schema::{ColumnDefault, IndexComponent, Maintain, Table}, value::{Value, InternalPrice}};
use super::word_heap as heap;
use crate::engine::authorized_scan::InternalLedger;

/// Cumulative callback work per source row. Admission adds one examination;
/// heap is checked separately because row scratch is released after each row.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Work {
    pub examined: u64,
    pub steps: u64,
    pub index_entries: u64,
}

impl Work {
    pub const DECODE: Self = Self { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 0 };

    pub fn with_contribution(mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Self {
        self.examined = self.examined.saturating_add(1);
        self.steps = self.steps.saturating_add(maintain.evaluation_steps());
        // A selected contribution creates exactly one entry, otherwise none.
        self.index_entries = self.index_entries.saturating_add(1);
        self
    }

    pub fn table(table: &Table) -> Self {
        table.indexes.values().fold(Self::DECODE, |work, index| match index.components.first() {
            Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => work.with_contribution(maintain),
            _ => work,
        })
    }

    fn counters(self, meter: &Meter) -> [(MeterKind, u64, u64, u64); 3] {
        [
            (MeterKind::Examined, self.examined.saturating_add(1), meter.used.examined, meter.ceilings.examined),
            (MeterKind::Steps, self.steps, meter.used.steps, meter.ceilings.steps),
            (MeterKind::IndexEntries, self.index_entries, meter.used.index_entries, meter.ceilings.index_entries),
        ]
    }

    pub fn limit(self, meter: &Meter, maximum: usize) -> usize {
        self.counters(meter).into_iter().filter(|(_, per_row, _, _)| *per_row != 0)
            .fold(maximum as u64, |limit, (_, per_row, used, ceiling)| limit.min(ceiling.saturating_sub(used) / per_row))
            // An empty range is still legal; a non-fitting singleton refuses
            // in fits(), after establishing that there really is a source row.
            .max(1) as usize
    }

    fn fits(self, meter: &Meter, count: usize) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        for (kind, per_row, used, ceiling) in self.counters(meter) {
            let actual = used.saturating_add(per_row.saturating_mul(count as u64));
            if actual > ceiling {
                if count > 1 { return Ok(false); }
                return Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind, actual, ceiling, site: meter.site().to_owned() });
            }
        }
        Ok(true)
    }
}

pub(crate) fn decode_bytes(data: &str) -> InternalPrice {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| heap::stored_row(data, scope).fixed(4096))
}

/// The price remains opaque: adoption may charge it only on its internal meter.
pub(crate) fn contribution_bytes(row: &Value, table: &Table) -> InternalPrice {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), |_, scope| {
        let mut bytes = row.retained_internal(scope);
        for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
            if row.field(name).is_ok() { continue; }
            let added = if table.maintained.contains_key(name) || kind.is_optional() { Some(InternalPrice::zero()) }
                else if let Some(ColumnDefault::Literal(value)) = table.defaults.get(name) { Some(value.retained_internal(scope)) }
                else { None };
            if let Some(added) = added { bytes = bytes.fixed(80 + name.len() as u64).plus(added); }
        }
        bytes.times(4).fixed(4096)
    })
}

pub(crate) fn charge(meter: &mut Meter, price: InternalPrice) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, scope| price.charge(meter, scope))
}
pub(crate) fn fits(meter: &mut Meter, price: &InternalPrice) -> bool {
    InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, scope| price.fits(meter, scope))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9.3 — shrink pages before adoption writes when retained images plus row work cannot fit.
#[cfg(feature="postgres")]
pub(crate) fn page_fits<'a>(images: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>, meter: &mut Meter,
    work: Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> InternalPrice>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    let checked=|row:&Value|Ok(scratch.map_or_else(InternalPrice::zero,|f|f(row)));
    page_fits_checked(images,meter,work,scratch.map(|_|&checked as &dyn Fn(&Value)->Result<InternalPrice,RuntimeError>))
}

pub(crate) fn page_fits_checked<'a>(images: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>, meter: &mut Meter,
    work: Work, scratch: Option<&dyn Fn(&Value) -> Result<InternalPrice,RuntimeError>>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    // Fix every cumulative budget before admission decodes or callbacks. Heap
    // retries retain used work, so both this check and limit use the remainder.
    if !work.fits(meter, images.len())? { return Ok(false); }
    let singleton = images.len() == 1;
    for data in images {
        let mark = meter.mark();
        let decode = decode_bytes(data);
        if !singleton && !fits(meter, &decode) { return Ok(false); }
        charge(meter, decode)?;
        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
        let row: Option<Value> = scratch.map(|_| crate::json_codec::from_text(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))).transpose()?;
        let work = match (scratch, row.as_ref()) { (Some(scratch), Some(row)) => scratch(row)?, _ => InternalPrice::zero() };
        let fits = fits(meter, &work);
        // Only a singleton may refuse for heap. Larger pages can be dropped
        // and fetched again with a smaller limit, without replaying a write.
        if !fits && singleton { charge(meter, work)?; }
        drop(row);
        meter.release_heap(mark);
        if !fits { return Ok(false); }
    }
    Ok(true)
}

/// Full simultaneous old/new key-vector scratch, including bounded token
/// cardinality. Live destinations are plain; captured/manual successors may
/// add word indexes and must still be admitted before native index_write.
pub(crate) fn index_capacity(table:&Table)->u64 {
    table.indexes.values().map(|i|index_copies(table,i)).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add)
}
fn index_copies(table:&Table,index:&crate::schema::Index)->u64 {
    if let Some((_,fields))=index.word_component() {
        fields.iter().filter_map(|f|table.columns.get(f)).map(|k|match k.required(){crate::schema::ColumnType::Text{max}=>u64::from(*max),crate::schema::ColumnType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().map(|s|s.len() as u64).max().unwrap_or(0),_=>0}).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add).min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64)
    }else{1}
}
pub(crate) fn index_scratch(name:&str,table:&Table)->u64 {
    table.indexes.iter().map(|(label,index)| {
        // Legacy oversized keys may legally remain equal or shrink. Their
        // buffers still coexist; the ordinary 2048-byte gate is not a bound
        // on allocation before that gate runs.
        let key=index.components.iter().fold(291_u64,|n,c|n.saturating_add(match c {
            IndexComponent::Column(field)=>table.columns.get(field).and_then(crate::schema::live::key_column).unwrap_or_else(||super::disclosed::decode_reservation(table)),
            IndexComponent::WordPrefixes{..}=>2*crate::words::MAX_TOKEN_BYTES as u64+3,
            _=>super::disclosed::decode_reservation(table),
        })).max(super::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as u64);
        // Empty token sets still allocate an IndexWrite slot and the word
        // field-reference vector. These are independent of emitted key count.
        let fixed=512_u64.saturating_add(4*(name.len()+label.len()) as u64)
            .saturating_add(index.word_component().map_or(0,|(_,fields)|(fields.len() as u64).saturating_mul(32)));
        fixed.saturating_add(index_copies(table,index).saturating_mul(key.saturating_mul(4).saturating_add(128*(index.components.len() as u64+1)+512+4*(name.len()+label.len()) as u64)))
    }).fold(0_u64,u64::saturating_add)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod live_index_scratch_tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn empty_word_sets_still_reserve_native_index_slots() {
        use crate::schema::{ColumnType,Index,IndexComponent,public_table};
        let table=public_table([("id".into(),ColumnType::Id),("body".into(),ColumnType::Text{max:0})].into(),[("words".into(),Index{components:vec![IndexComponent::WordPrefixes{fields:vec!["body".into()],contract:serde_json::Value::String(crate::words::CONTRACT.into())},IndexComponent::Column("id".into())],unique:false})].into());
        assert_eq!(index_capacity(&table),0);
        // A nonempty vector of zero-key IndexWrite records remains retained.
        assert!(index_scratch("t",&table)>=512);
    }
    #[test]
    fn enum_words_reserve_the_tokens_the_native_index_will_emit() {
        use crate::schema::{ColumnType,Index,IndexComponent,public_table};
        let table=public_table([("id".into(),ColumnType::Id),("body".into(),ColumnType::Enum{variants:vec!["one two".into()]})].into(),[("words".into(),Index{components:vec![IndexComponent::WordPrefixes{fields:vec!["body".into()],contract:serde_json::Value::String(crate::words::CONTRACT.into())},IndexComponent::Column("id".into())],unique:false})].into());
        let row=crate::value::object([("id",Value::Id("r".into())),("body",Value::String("one two".into()))]);
        let keys=super::super::index_keys(&table.indexes["words"],&row,"r");assert_eq!(keys.len(),2);
        assert!(index_capacity(&table)>=keys.len() as u64);
        assert!(index_scratch("t",&table)>=keys.iter().map(|k|k.len() as u64*4).sum());
    }
}

//! Read-only durable metadata and request store binding.
use super::*;

pub(super) fn response_head(engine: &mut Engine) -> Result<(String, u64), Refusal> {
    let tx = engine.store_mut().read_transaction()?;
    let id: String = tx.store_id()?;
    Ok((id, tx.next_seq()? - 1))

// @ref LLP 3000.013#6 — a replay belongs to its acknowledged store, even if
// the endpoint changes between the client's probe and this transaction.
pub(super) fn intent_store(engine: &Engine, payload: &Json) -> Result<(), Refusal> {
    let Some(expected) = payload.get("store_id").filter(|id| !id.is_null()) else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let current = engine.store().store_identity()?;
    if expected
        .as_str()
        .is_some_and(|id| Some(id) == current.as_deref())
    {
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(Refusal::new(
        "E_STORE_REPLACED",
        "store",
        "the intent belongs to another store; its original outcome is unknown",
    )
    .site("request.store_id")
    .rewrite("reconcile this write with its original store before submitting new intent")
    .guide("sync"))
}

// Typed mutation inputs have one terminal failure envelope, including wire decoding.
pub(super) fn argument_refusal(request:Request,shared:&Shared,id:Option<&str>,why:Refusal){
    if !request.url().starts_with("/m/") {return operation_refusal(request,shared,400,why);}
    match shared.read_identity() {
        Ok((store_id,head,generation))=>{
            let mut reply=json!({"state":"failed","why":refusal_json(&why),"store_id":store_id,"head":head,"generation":generation});
            if let Some(id)=id {reply["id"]=json!(id);}
            respond_timed(request,shared,200,reply);
        }
        Err(error)=>respond_timed(request,shared,503,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — reconcile the exact bearer before the SDK observes advanced business time.
pub(super) fn session_clock_headers(request: &Request, shared: &Shared) -> Vec<Header> {
    if !shared.staging && !shared.personas { return clock_headers(shared).into(); }
    let Ok(token) = crate::auth::bearer_token(request) else { return clock_headers(shared).into(); };
    // Detached readers never fall back to the writer: callers may still hold it.
    // Keep the process clock fixed across the committed authority snapshot, so
    // preserved lifetime and the clock stamp describe the same staging jump.
    let Ok((epoch, reader)) = shared.reader() else {
        return vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "unavailable").unwrap()];
    };
    let identity = lock(&shared.wake).store_id.clone();
    let clock = lock(&shared.clock);
    let now = clock.now().max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    let timing = identity.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| snapback4_core::RuntimeError::Auth("store identity unavailable".into()))
        .and_then(|identity| reader.staging_session_timing(token, now, identity));
    let headers = match timing {
        Ok(timing) => {
            let mut headers = vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "staging").unwrap(),
                Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Time", now.to_string()).unwrap(),
                Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Clock", clock.revision()).unwrap()];
            if let Some(timing) = timing {
                headers.push(Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Expires", timing.expires_at.to_string()).unwrap());
                if let Some(cap) = timing.cap_expires_at { headers.push(Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Cap", cap.to_string()).unwrap()); }
            }
            headers
        }
        Err(_) => vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Session-Timing", "unavailable").unwrap()],
    };
    drop(clock);
    lock(&shared.readers).put(&epoch, reader.into_inner());
    headers
}

pub(crate) fn clock_headers(shared: &Shared) -> [Header; 2] {
    let clock = lock(&shared.clock);
    let now = clock.now().max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(Ordering::Acquire));
    [Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Time", now.to_string()).unwrap(),
     Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Clock", clock.revision()).unwrap()]
}

// @ref LLP 3000.017#3.3 — advertise only on ephemeral backends; durable-only HTTP bytes stay unchanged.
// The online tier can discover /schema facts through its ordinary traffic.
pub(crate) fn ephemeral_headers(shared: &Shared) -> Vec<Header> {
    if lock(&shared.wake).eph.tables.is_empty() { return Vec::new(); }
    vec![Header::from_bytes("X-Snapback-Ephemeral", "1").unwrap(),
         Header::from_bytes("Access-Control-Expose-Headers", "X-Snapback-Ephemeral").unwrap()]
}

// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#8 — absent request ids stay absent; result.id is the row id.
pub(crate) fn mutation_reply(mut body: Json) -> Json {
    if body.get("id").is_some_and(Json::is_null) { body.as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("id"); }
    body
}

    fn default() -> Self {

/// Keep baseline nominal types in their own namespace: a table may no longer
/// exist, or may now have a different public row shape.
fn baseline_type(ty: &Ty) -> String {
    match ty {
        Ty::Row(table) => format!("BaselineRows[{}]", string_literal(table)),
        Ty::WriteRow(table) => format!("BaselineWriteRows[{}]", string_literal(table)),
        Ty::Page(table, _) => format!("BaselineRows[{}][]", string_literal(table)),
        Ty::Optional(inner) => format!("{} | null", baseline_type(inner)),
        Ty::List(inner, _) | Ty::Collection(inner, _) => format!("Array<{}>", baseline_type(inner)),
        Ty::Object(fields) | Ty::RowShape(fields) | Ty::RowObject(fields) => {
            let mut parts = fields.iter().map(|(name, ty)| format!("{}{}: {}", property(name), if matches!(ty,Ty::Omittable(_)){"?"}else{""}, baseline_type(ty))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if matches!(ty, Ty::RowShape(_) | Ty::RowObject(_)) { parts.push("pending?: boolean".into()); parts.push("retained?: boolean".into()); }
            if parts.is_empty() { "Record<string, never>".into() } else { format!("{{ {} }}", parts.join("; ")) }
        }
        _ => ty_ts(ty),
    }
}

    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    ("release-backfills-v4", |s| !s.downfills.is_empty()),
    ("live-parent-copy-v1", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.live.is_some()))),
    ("source-write-reservations-v2", |s| s.source_reservations.values().any(|p| p.birth.is_some())),
    ("source-write-reservations-v1", |s| !s.source_reservations.is_empty()),
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — older devices must not execute newly eligible
    // writes using their receipt-derived maintenance path.
    ("receipt-derived-prediction-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| s.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target))
        || s.has_receipt_columns()),
    ("rule-reference-v2", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t|
        [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.any_term(&|term| matches!(term, RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. })))
        || t.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { key, .. } if key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some()))))),
    ("rule-reference", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.has_reference()))),
    ("declarative-receipts-v4", |s| !s.receipts.is_empty()),
    ("owner-key-coverage", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.own_keys.is_some())),
    ("ephemeral", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.ephemeral.is_some())),
    ("field-authority", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.written_by.is_empty() || t.update_transition)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — an older decoder refuses ordered insert rules rather than misjudging them.
    ("insert-rule-order", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered(&t.rules.insert))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a decoder that orders only int/time in insert rules refuses a money or decimal order by name.
    ("insert-rule-order-units", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered_units(t, &t.rules.insert))),
    ("row-keyed-view", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — older devices compute canonical-JSON
    // aggregate ids and would silently miss digest-addressed target rows.
    ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.is_none())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#8 — an older engine or device must not delete with the old (orphaning) semantics.
    ("reference-actions", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.on_delete.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — pre-Wave-12 devices neither retire expiry
    // through actions nor queue an unproved same-id physical predecessor.
    ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", |s| s.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.is_expiring() && s.is_referenced(name))),
    ("read-through", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.through.is_some()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.parent_key.is_some() || !m.aliases.is_empty())),
    // Device projections keep column metadata but omit private maintains.
    ("maintained-column", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.maintained.is_empty()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.is_some())),
    ("recorded-attribution", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.recorded.is_empty())),
    ("sequence-by", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.sequences.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — an older decoder names the bounded int it cannot check.
    ("int-range", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.values().any(int_range))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — civil keys and calendar schedules.
    ("calendar-month", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.indexes.values().any(|i| i.components.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Calendar(key) if key.civil()))))
        || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.computed.values().any(|key| key.civil()))),
    ("calendar-schedule", |s| s.schedules.iter().any(|schedule| schedule.months > 0)),
    ("timeline", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 1)),
    ("timeline-v2", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 2)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#3 — an older device would page a merged plan as an eager merge and refuse its server cursors; it refuses the backend by name.
    ("branch-merge-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_merge)),
    ("branch-membership-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#15 — v2 fences metered uncapped discovery and row-id point lanes from v1 devices.
    ("branch-pages-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v2)),
    ("branch-pages-v3", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v3)),
    ("branch-pages-v5", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v5)),
    ("branch-pages-v4", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v4)),
    ("branch-membership-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership_v2)),
    // Source slots alter negative coverage, prediction and application row projection.
    ("timeline-event-slots", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.keys().any(|field| timeline::is_slot(field)))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.3 — a decoder that ignored `also` would hold only the first arm and lose rows.
    ("union-audience", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(Sync::is_union))),
    ("time-audiences-v1", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some())),
];

fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match kind {
        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

impl Schema {
    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
    }
    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
    }
}

impl Serialize for Schema {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        let required = self.required_capabilities();
        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
        let mut wire = self.clone();
        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
        }
        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut carriers = 0;
        let mut legacy = false;
        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
            let mut recorded = 0;
            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
                    carriers += 1;
                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
                    false
                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
                    recorded += 1;
                    false
                } else { true }
            });
            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
            }
            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
        }
        for name in &declared {
            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
            }
        }
        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
            else { required.remove(cap); }
        }
        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
        }
        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
        }
        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
        }
        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
        }
        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
        Ok(schema)
    }
}
